stages.label: 1991 Watershed & Rao Era
stages.detail: Five years that turned India inside out. Rajiv assassinated 21 May 1991; Chandra Shekhar caretaker until June. Narasimha Rao + Manmohan Singh launch LPG reforms (24 July 1991 budget): industrial licence raj abolished, rupee devalued, MRTP cap removed, FDI opened. Babri demolished 6 Dec 1992; communal riots; 1993 Mumbai blasts. Indra Sawhney upholds 27% OBC reservation. 73rd-74th Amendments constitutionalise local government. WTO accession 1995. End of one-party dominance.

stages.label: Coalition Instability: United Front
stages.detail: Two years of fragile centre. 1996 election produces hung parliament. BJP's 13-day Vajpayee government falls. United Front (Janata Dal + 12 regional parties + Left, supported by Congress) governs under Deve Gowda (June 1996 - April 1997), then I.K. Gujral (April 1997 - March 1998). Gujral Doctrine on neighbours. Congress withdraws support over CBI/DMK; March 1998 mid-term polls.

stages.label: Vajpayee NDA & Nuclear India
stages.detail: BJP-led NDA full term — 13 months 1998-99 then 1999-2004. Pokhran-II (11-13 May 1998) declares India nuclear weapons state; US/Japan sanctions. Lahore Bus Yatra Feb 1999 → Kargil War May-July 1999. IC-814 hijacking Dec 1999. Parliament attack 13 Dec 2001; Operation Parakram 2001-02. Gujarat riots Feb-Mar 2002. Golden Quadrilateral, Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan, POTA 2002, RTE Article 21A (86th Amendment). India Shining 2004 ad campaign loses.

stages.label: UPA-I: Reform with Human Face
stages.detail: UPA-I governs with Left Front external support. Sonia Gandhi declines PM, names Manmohan Singh. National Advisory Council drives rights-based architecture. RTI Act 2005, NREGA 2005, Forest Rights Act 2006, Domestic Violence Act 2005, Hindu Succession Amendment 2005, Sachar Committee 2006, Ministry of Minority Affairs 2006. POTA repealed; UAPA expanded. Indo-US Civil Nuclear Deal 2005-08; NSG waiver 6 Sept 2008; trust vote 22 July 2008. 26/11 Mumbai attacks Nov 2008. NIA created.

stages.label: UPA-II & Anti-Corruption Wave
stages.detail: UPA-II (Manmohan PM 2009-14) battered by scams: 2G, CWG 2010, Coalgate. Anna Hazare anti-corruption movement Aug 2011 → Lokpal Act 2013. Aam Aadmi Party born. Nirbhaya Dec 2012 → Criminal Law Amendment 2013. Aadhaar enrolment, DBT pilot. Food Security Act 2013, Land Acquisition Act 2013. NJAC enacted 2014 (struck down 2015). Modi wave: 2014 election, BJP 282 seats — first single-party majority since 1984.

stages.label: Modi-I: Flagship Rollouts (GST, Demonetisation)
stages.detail: Modi I — flagship rollouts. Jan Dhan (Aug 2014), Swachh Bharat (Oct 2014), Make in India (Sept 2014), Mudra (April 2015), NITI Aayog (Jan 2015 replaces Planning Commission). Demonetisation 8 Nov 2016 voids 86% currency. GST live 1 July 2017 (101st Amendment). RBI MPC + inflation targeting 2016. AQR 2015 → IBC 2016 → bank mergers. Surgical Strikes Sept 2016 + Balakot Feb 2019. Triple Talaq (SC 2017, Act 2019). Ayushman Bharat Sept 2018.

stages.label: Modi-II: Art 370, CAA, COVID, Farm Laws
stages.detail: Modi II returns with 303 seats. Article 370 abrogated 5 Aug 2019 + J&K bifurcated. CAA 2019 + Shaheen Bagh protests. COVID-19 lockdown 25 March 2020 + migrant crisis. Atmanirbhar Bharat May 2020. Vaccine rollout 16 Jan 2021 — Covaxin/Covishield. Farm Laws Sept 2020 → 13-month protests → repealed Nov 2021. Pegasus, electoral bonds debate. PLI schemes. G20 Presidency Dec 2022-Nov 2023; Delhi Declaration. Chandrayaan-3 lunar landing 23 Aug 2023. New criminal laws (BNS/BNSS/BSA) 2023. Women's Reservation Act 2023. Article 370 SC verdict Dec 2023. 2024 election: NDA 293, BJP 240 (lost majority).

stages.label: Modi-III & Current Affairs
stages.detail: Modi III — coalition dependence renewed. Ram Mandir consecration 22 Jan 2024 (pre-election). Waqf Amendment Act 2024. Bangladesh regime change Aug 2024 (Sheikh Hasina ouster). Maharashtra/Jharkhand polls; Delhi Assembly BJP win Feb 2025. Mahakumbh 2025 (~66 crore footfall). Aviation/manufacturing PLI scaled. Current affairs to UPSC May 2026.

stages.label: Kashmir & Punjab Crises
stages.detail: Two parallel internal-security theatres. Kashmir Insurgency from 1989 (JKLF, Hizbul Mujahideen); Pandit exodus Jan-Mar 1990. Governor's rule under Jagmohan. ~80,000 killed by 2010. Punjab militancy ended early 1990s by KPS Gill-led police. Beant Singh CM 1992, assassinated 1995. Article 370 abrogated 2019; J&K reorganised; SC upholds 2023.

stages.label: Terrorism: Parliament, 26/11, Pulwama
stages.detail: Era of mega-attacks. Parliament attack 13 Dec 2001 → Operation Parakram. 26/11 Mumbai 2008 (Lashkar). Pune German Bakery 2010, Delhi blasts. Pathankot Jan 2016. Uri attack Sept 2016 → surgical strikes. Pulwama 14 Feb 2019 (40 CRPF) → Balakot air strike 26 Feb 2019. NIA Act 2008/2019 expansion. UAPA amendments 2008/2012/2019. Counterterror architecture matures.

stages.label: Constitutional Amendments 65-106
stages.detail: 33 amendments in 33 years (1990-2023). 65th creates NCSC/NCST combined commission. 69th gives Delhi NCT special status. 71st/92nd add 4+4 languages to 8th Schedule. 73rd/74th constitutionalise PRIs/ULBs. 76th-95th cycle of reservation extensions, delimitation freezes. 86th adds Article 21A. 91st caps CoM at 15% + closes anti-defection loopholes. 99th NJAC struck down. 100th India-Bangladesh land swap. 101st GST. 102nd-105th NCBC + state OBC tussle. 103rd 10% EWS. 106th Women's Reservation 2023.

stages.label: Landmark SC Cases (1994-2024)
stages.detail: Era of basic-structure refinement. S.R. Bommai 1994 — federalism, secularism, judicial review of Article 356. Vishaka 1997 — workplace harassment. L. Chandra Kumar 1997 — judicial review of tribunals. M. Nagaraj 2006 — promotion reservation conditions. I.R. Coelho 2007 — 9th Schedule open to review post-1973. NJAC 2015 — collegium revived. Puttaswamy 2017 — privacy fundamental right. Triple Talaq, Aadhaar, Section 377 (Navtej), Section 497 (Joseph Shine), Sabarimala — all 2017-18. Article 370 case 2023. Electoral Bonds 2024.

stages.label: Constitutional & Statutory Institutions
stages.detail: Two waves of institution-building. Wave I (1990s-2000s): NCW 1992, NHRC 1993, NCBC 1993, CIC 2005, NCST 2004, NCPCR 2007, NIA 2008, UIDAI 2009. Wave II (2010s-2020s): NGT 2010, Lokpal Act 2013/Lokpal 2014, NITI Aayog Jan 2015 (replaces Planning Commission), GST Council 2016, NCLT/NCLAT 2016, NFRA 2018, CDS Jan 2020. State counterparts: SHRCs, SECs, SFCs.

stages.label: Electoral & Criminal Law Reforms
stages.detail: Multi-member EC 1993 (Seshan era). NOTA 2013, VVPAT 2013 → universal 2019. Aadhaar Act 2016 (Money Bill). Electoral Bonds 2017 → struck down 2024. CEC Appointment Act 2023 replaces SC's Anoop Baranwal mechanism. POTA 2002 → repealed 2004 → UAPA expansion. Three new criminal laws 2023 (BNS, BNSS, BSA) replace IPC, CrPC, Evidence Act 1872 — effective 1 July 2024.

stages.label: Economic Reforms I: LPG Architecture (1991-99)
stages.detail: First-generation reforms 1991-99. Industrial Policy 24 July 1991 abolishes licence raj for most sectors. Rupee devalued 20%. MRTP modified. SEBI made statutory 1992. Capital Issues (Control) Act repealed 1992. FII access 1992. NSE launched 1994. WTO accession 1 Jan 1995. Navaratnas 1997, Mini Ratnas 1997. FEMA 1999 replaces FERA. 8th-9th Five-Year Plans average 6.94% then 5.5% growth. Chelliah Tax Reform Committee.

stages.label: Economic Reforms II: New Millennium (2000-13)
stages.detail: Reform consolidation 2000-13. QR removal April 2001 (WTO compliance). SEZ Act 2005, MGNREGA 2005, RTI 2005. FRBMA 2003. Competition Act 2002, CCI operational 2009. Maharatnas 2010. NFSA 2013, Land Acquisition Act 2013. DBT pilot 2013. 10th-12th Five-Year Plans average 7.6%-7.9%-6.7%. Taper tantrum 2013 — Raghuram Rajan takes RBI charge. Twelfth Plan is the last (post-2017 NITI Aayog 3-year action agendas).

stages.label: Economic Reforms III: Modi Era (2014-25)
stages.detail: Modi-era reforms. Planning Commission abolished 2014; NITI Aayog Jan 2015. Sovereign Gold Bonds 2015. Make in India, Skill India, Digital India 2015. UDAY 2015 (DISCOM debt). Demonetisation Nov 2016. GST Jul 2017. PLI launched 2020 (14 sectors). Atmanirbhar Bharat May 2020 (Rs 20L cr). PMGKAY 2020 + COVID stimulus. PM Gati Shakti 2021. National Logistics Policy 2022. Ease of Doing Business 142→63. Indian economy: 5th largest by 2024 ($3.7T).

stages.label: Banking & Financial Sector Reforms
stages.detail: Banking architecture transformed. Narasimham I 1991 + II 1998 reports drive financial-sector reform. Private bank licences 1993 (HDFC/ICICI/Axis/IndusInd). MPC 2016 — 6 members vote on repo. Flexible inflation targeting (CPI 4±2%) RBI Act amendment 2016. AQR July 2015 — NPA crisis revealed. IBC 2016 + IBBI. PSB mega-mergers 2017-2020 — 27 banks → 12. Bank recapitalisation rounds. Raghuram Rajan, Urjit Patel, Shaktikanta Das.

stages.label: Social Justice & Reservation
stages.detail: Mandal-era reservation politics. Mandal Commission report 1980; implementation Aug 1990 → Indra Sawhney 1992 (50% cap, creamy layer). 77th, 81st, 85th Amendments + 117th Bill on promotion reservation. 27% OBC in higher education from 2007 (93rd Amendment 2005, Ashoka Thakur 2008). 103rd Amendment 2019 — 10% EWS. 102nd/105th NCBC + state OBC powers. SC/ST Atrocities Act 1989. Forest Rights Act 2006 (tribal land). BSP/Kanshi Ram → Mayawati. Dalit identity politics.

stages.label: Women's Rights & Gender
stages.detail: Post-Shah Bano framework. Muslim Women Act 1986 → Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act 2019 (triple talaq). Vishaka 1997 → POSH Act 2013. Domestic Violence Act 2005. Hindu Succession Amendment 2005 — daughters equal coparceners. Beti Bachao Beti Padhao 2015 (declining sex ratio). Nirbhaya Dec 2012 → Criminal Law Amendment 2013 (acid attack, voyeurism, stalking new offences). 33% Women's Reservation Act 2023 (post-delimitation effect).

stages.label: Foreign Policy & Diplomacy
stages.detail: Multi-aligned diplomacy. End of Soviet Union forced reset 1991. Look East Policy 1991 (PV Narasimha Rao) → Act East 2014 (Modi). India-US: Clinton visit March 2000 — first since Carter. Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement 2000. Civil Nuclear Deal 2005-08. India-Israel established 1992; Indo-Pacific framework. SAARC, BIMSTEC, BRICS (2006), SCO (2017). G20 Presidency 2022-23. Permanent UNSC seat bid (G4). Israel-Hamas, Russia-Ukraine balancing 2022+.

stages.label: Environment & Climate
stages.detail: Climate framework era. Earth Summit Rio 1992 → UNFCCC + CBD. Kyoto 1997. India INDC Oct 2015 (Paris). India Updated NDC Aug 2022 — 50% non-fossil capacity, 45% emissions intensity cut by 2030, Net Zero 2070 (Panchamrit). ISA launched 2015 with France. NAPCC 2008 (8 missions: Solar, EE, Habitat, Water, Himalayan, Green India, Agriculture, Knowledge). Biological Diversity Act 2002, NGT 2010, CAMPA 2016, Namami Gange 2014. India 80+ Ramsar sites by 2024.

stages.label: Science, Technology & Space
stages.detail: Pokhran-II 1998 ends nuclear ambiguity. Indo-US Nuclear Deal 2008. ISRO milestones: Chandrayaan-1 (2008, water on Moon), Mangalyaan (2014, Mars first try), Chandrayaan-2 (2019, lander failed), Chandrayaan-3 (Aug 2023, south-pole landing first), Aditya-L1 (2023, Sun observation). National Space Day 23 Aug. National Quantum Mission 2023. Gaganyaan crewed 2026. Private space sector opened 2020 (Skyroot, Pixxel, Agnikul). National Space Policy 2023.

stages.label: Digital India & Payments
stages.detail: Digital revolution. Aadhaar from 2010 onwards. NPCI 2008 → IMPS, RuPay (2012), UPI (2016 → 14B+ monthly transactions by 2024). Digital India 2015 — DigiLocker, MyGov, BharatNet. JAM trinity (Jan Dhan + Aadhaar + Mobile) — DBT backbone for Rs 34L cr. 5G rollout from October 2022 — fastest globally. UPI internationalisation (Singapore, France, UAE). India's Digital Public Infrastructure as G20 export 2023.

stages.label: Culture & Heritage (UNESCO)
stages.detail: UNESCO recognition era. World Heritage Sites: Qutb Minar + Humayun's Tomb (1993), Bhimbetka (2003), CST (2004), Red Fort (2007), Western Ghats (2012), Hill Forts of Rajasthan (2013), Rani ki Vav (2014), Nalanda + Le Corbusier Chandigarh (2016), Ahmedabad first Indian city (2017), Jaipur city (2019), Dholavira + Kakatiya (2021), Santiniketan + Hoysala temples (2023), Charaideo Moidams (2024). UNESCO ICH inscriptions 2008-2023: Kutiyattam, Ramlila, Vedic chanting, Yoga (2016), Kumbh Mela (2017), Durga Puja Kolkata (2021), Garba (2023). GI Act 1999.

stages.label: Parallel — End of Cold War & Post-Soviet Russia
stages.detail: Berlin Wall falls 9 Nov 1989 → 1990 unification. USSR dissolves 26 Dec 1991. Gorbachev's perestroika/glasnost (1985-91) trigger nationalist surge. Yeltsin shock therapy. CIS formed Dec 1991. Yugoslavia breaks up; Bosnian war. EU formed Maastricht 1992. First Gulf War 1991. Chemical Weapons Convention 1992. Russia-NATO uneasy peace. India loses Soviet ally; pivots to multipolar diplomacy.

stages.label: Parallel — 9/11 & War on Terror
stages.detail: 9/11 attacks 11 Sept 2001 reshape world order. US launches Operation Enduring Freedom (Afghanistan) Oct 2001 → Taliban falls Dec 2001. Al-Qaeda hunted. Operation Iraqi Freedom March 2003 — toppled Saddam, no WMDs found. Musharraf coup Pakistan Oct 1999; ally in War on Terror. Kosovo crisis 1999. India-US engagement deepens via War on Terror frame. Bin Laden killed May 2011 in Abbottabad raid.

stages.label: Parallel — 2008 Global Financial Crisis
stages.detail: Lehman Brothers collapse 15 Sept 2008 triggers global recession. Credit freeze, bank failures across US/Europe. India weathers via insulated banking, domestic demand. RBI cuts repo from 9% to 4.75% (Oct 2008-Apr 2009). Three fiscal stimulus packages Dec 2008-Feb 2009. GDP slows 9.3%→6.7% but rebounds. Foundation of expansionary trend that turned into 2013 taper tantrum and twin balance sheet problem.

stages.label: Parallel — COVID-19 Pandemic
stages.detail: COVID-19 declared pandemic 11 Mar 2020. India lockdown 25 March 2020 — strictest globally. Migrant labour reverse-migration. PMGKAY food relief. Delta wave April-June 2021 (Kumbh + WB elections super-spreaders). Vaccination drive 16 Jan 2021 — Covaxin (indigenous), Covishield (SII-AstraZeneca). 220 crore+ doses by 2023. Co-WIN platform. Economic contraction FY21 (-6.6%, first since 1979). India world's pharmacy: 'vaccine maitri' diplomacy. Atmanirbhar Bharat response.

stages.label: Parallel — Recent World (Arab Spring → Trump → Russia-Ukraine → Israel-Hamas)
stages.detail: Major global currents bridging India's Modi era. Arab Spring (2010-12) → Egypt/Libya/Tunisia/Yemen regime change → Syrian Civil War + ISIS rise (2014, fall 2019). Snowden leaks 2013. Brexit referendum 2016, UK leaves EU 31 Jan 2020. Trump-I (2017-21) — Howdy Modi, Namaste Trump, Abraham Accords. COVID-19 reshapes geopolitics 2020. Russia invades Ukraine 24 Feb 2022 — energy crisis, food crisis. Sri Lanka collapse April 2022. Israel-Hamas war from 7 Oct 2023. Trump-II re-elected Nov 2024 (inaugurated Jan 2025) — global tariffs.

nodes.label: MNCs and Modern Globalisation
nodes.detail: MNCs first 1920s. Spread 1950s-60s. Late-1970s shifted production to low-wage Asia. China's post-1979 opening transformed global economy.

nodes.label: Rajiv Gandhi Assassination (21 May 1991)
nodes.detail: Assassinated 21 May 1991 at Sriperumbudur, Tamil Nadu during 1991 campaign. LTTE suicide bomber Thenmozhi Rajaratnam ('Dhanu') detonated RDX vest during garland presentation. Revenge for IPKF 1987-90. Led to Congress sympathy wave, Narasimha Rao became PM 21 June 1991. Jain Commission investigated.

nodes.label: Chandra Shekhar (Interim PM, Nov 1990 - Jun 1991)
nodes.detail: 8th PM of India, 10 Nov 1990 - 21 Jun 1991. Janata Dal (S) leader, 64 MPs with Congress outside support. Bhrought during Mandal-Rath Yatra crisis. Authorised gold-pledge to BOP crisis (47 tons to Bank of England May 1991). Lost when Congress withdrew support March 1991. Caretaker till Rao.

nodes.label: Babri Masjid Demolition (6 Dec 1992)
nodes.detail: 16th-century mosque demolished by VHP/Bajrang Dal kar sevaks at Ayodhya on 6 Dec 1992. Built 1528 under Mir Baqi (Babur's commander). Kar Seva organised by VHP-BJP after Dec 1990 suspension of kar seva. Kalyan Singh UP CM (BJP) resigned. Riots across India (~2,000 killed). 1993 Mumbai blasts retaliation. 2019 SC verdict awarded site for Ram temple.

nodes.label: P.V. Narasimha Rao (PM 1991-96)
nodes.detail: 9th PM, 21 June 1991 - 16 May 1996. Congress. Presided over LPG reforms (Manmohan Singh FM). Handled Babri demolition Dec 1992 + 1993 Mumbai blasts. Look East Policy 1992. Issued Panchayati Raj 73rd + 74th Amendments April 1993. First PM outside Nehru-Gandhi family to serve full 5-year term.

nodes.label: 1991 Lok Sabha Elections
nodes.detail: Held May-June 1991, disrupted by Rajiv's assassination 21 May. Congress (I) 232 seats under sympathy wave (pre-assassination estimate was 120-130). BJP 120 (up from 85), National Front 59, Left 49, Janata Dal 59. Narasimha Rao PM 21 June 1991. First minority Congress govt survived full term via internal coalitions.

nodes.label: 73rd and 74th Constitutional Amendments
nodes.detail: Passed in 1992 to constitutionalise local self-government. Made regular elections to local bodies mandatory. Reserved one-third seats for women. Created State Election Commission for local elections. Gave constitutional status to panchayats and municipalities.

nodes.label: Dalit Rights Movement
nodes.detail: Movement for rights and dignity of Dalits (formerly called untouchables) in India. Seeks to end caste discrimination. Some groups sought international attention by raising caste at UN Conference Against Racism in Durban (2001). Political expression has led to reservations and anti-discrimination laws.

nodes.label: Nepal's Movement for Democracy (2006)
nodes.detail: King Gyanendra dismissed PM and dissolved Parliament in February 2005. Seven Party Alliance (SPA) called indefinite strike in April 2006, joined by Maoists. 3-5 lakh protesters. King forced to concede: restored Parliament, all-party government, new Constituent Assembly. SPA chose Girija Prasad Koirala as PM.

nodes.label: Bolivia's Water War (2000)
nodes.detail: World Bank pressured Bolivia to privatise water supply. MNC raised prices 4 times in Cochabamba. FEDECOR-led alliance of workers, farmers, students organised strikes. Government imposed martial law. People forced MNC to flee, contract cancelled, water restored to municipality at old rates.

nodes.label: Narmada Bachao Andolan
nodes.detail: Movement opposing the Sardar Sarovar Dam on river Narmada. Led by Medha Patkar. Raised issues of displacement, environmental destruction, and rehabilitation. Example of a movement group that combines environmental concerns with social justice. Influenced dam height and rehabilitation policies.

nodes.label: Right to Information Movement
nodes.detail: Movement for citizens' right to access government information. Led to enactment of Right to Information Act (RTI Act, 2005). MKSS (Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan) in Rajasthan was a key organisation. RTI became a powerful tool for transparency and accountability.

nodes.label: Seven Party Alliance (Nepal)
nodes.detail: Alliance of major political parties in Nepal's Parliament that led the 2006 democracy movement. Joined by Maoists, labour unions, indigenous peoples' organisations, teachers, lawyers, and human rights groups. Showed how diverse organisations unite for democratic goals.

nodes.label: FEDECOR (Bolivia)
nodes.detail: Organisation of local professionals (engineers, environmentalists) that led Bolivia's water war. Supported by farmers' federation, factory workers' unions, university students, and homeless children. Socialist Party also supported the movement, later came to power in 2006.

nodes.label: Article 21 - Right to Life
nodes.detail: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except according to procedure established by law. Expanded by SC to include right to livelihood, education, health, clean environment, privacy, dignity. Most expansively interpreted article.

nodes.label: Indra Sawhney Case (1992)
nodes.detail: Mandal Commission case. SC upheld 27% OBC reservation but capped total reservation at 50%. Introduced 'creamy layer' concept — economically advanced sections of backward classes excluded from reservation.

nodes.label: 91st Amendment (2003)
nodes.detail: Limited size of Council of Ministers to 15% of total Lok Sabha/Assembly strength. Also strengthened anti-defection provisions. Aimed at preventing oversized ministries used as patronage.

nodes.label: Justice Ramaswamy Impeachment (1993)
nodes.detail: First and only impeachment motion against a Supreme Court judge. Justice V. Ramaswamy was accused of misappropriating funds as Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana HC. Inquiry commission found him guilty. Motion got required two-thirds of those voting but failed because Congress abstained, so it did not get majority of total strength of the House.

nodes.label: Creation of New States (2000)
nodes.detail: In the 1990s, larger states were divided for administrative efficiency and to meet demands for separate statehood. Bihar divided to create Jharkhand, UP to create Uttaranchal (now Uttarakhand), Madhya Pradesh to create Chhattisgarh. All three new states created in November 2000.

nodes.label: 73rd Constitutional Amendment (1992)
nodes.detail: Passed in 1992, came into force in 1993. Provides constitutional status to Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs). Creates uniform three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat, Block/Mandal Panchayat, Zilla Panchayat. Mandates direct elections, 5-year term, one-third reservation for women, reservations for SC/ST, Gram Sabha, State Election Commissioner, and State Finance Commission. Added Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects.

nodes.label: 74th Constitutional Amendment (1992)
nodes.detail: Passed in 1992, came into force in 1993. Provides constitutional status to urban local bodies (Nagarpalikas). Mirrors provisions of 73rd amendment for urban areas: direct elections, reservations, State Election Commission, State Finance Commission. Added Twelfth Schedule listing functions of municipalities. Applies to Nagar Panchayats, Municipal Councils, and Municipal Corporations.

nodes.label: Reservation for Women in Local Bodies
nodes.detail: One-third of all positions in panchayat institutions reserved for women. Applies not just to ordinary members but also to positions of Chairpersons/Adhyakshas at all three levels. Reservation within reserved categories too -- a seat may be reserved for both woman and SC/ST simultaneously. Over 10 lakh women elected to local bodies. Over 80,000 women Sarpanchas.

nodes.label: Reservation for SC/ST in Local Bodies
nodes.detail: Reservations for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes at all three levels of Panchayati Raj in proportion to their population. Applies to positions of Chairpersons also. States can additionally provide for OBC reservations. About 6.6 lakh elected members from SC/ST communities in urban and local bodies. Has significantly altered social profile of local bodies.

nodes.label: Eleventh Schedule
nodes.detail: Added by the 73rd Amendment. Lists 29 subjects to be transferred to Panchayati Raj institutions from the State List. Includes agriculture, minor irrigation, rural housing, drinking water, roads, rural electrification, poverty alleviation, education, health and sanitation, family welfare, women and child development, public distribution system. Actual transfer depends on state legislation.

nodes.label: Twelfth Schedule
nodes.detail: Added by the 74th Amendment. Lists 18 functions to be transferred to urban local bodies (Nagarpalikas). Includes urban planning, regulation of land use, public health, water supply, fire services, urban forestry, slum improvement, urban poverty alleviation, provision of urban amenities. Actual devolution depends on state legislation.

nodes.label: State Election Commissioner
nodes.detail: State government required to appoint a State Election Commissioner responsible for conducting elections to Panchayati Raj institutions and urban local bodies. Office is autonomous like the Election Commission of India. However, SEC is an independent officer not linked to or under the control of ECI. Ensures regular and fair elections to local bodies.

nodes.label: State Finance Commission
nodes.detail: State government required to appoint a State Finance Commission every five years. Examines financial position of local governments. Reviews distribution of revenues between state and local governments, and between rural and urban local governments. Ensures allocation of funds to local bodies is not merely a political matter. Recommends principles for tax sharing with panchayats.

nodes.label: Five-Year Term for Panchayats
nodes.detail: Each Panchayat body has a fixed term of five years. If dissolved before completing its term, fresh elections must be held within six months. This is a crucial provision ensuring continuous existence of elected local bodies. Before the 73rd amendment, elections were often postponed indefinitely in many states.

nodes.label: PESA Act (1996)
nodes.detail: Panchayats (Extension to Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996. Extended provisions of Panchayat system to Adivasi/tribal areas. Protects rights of tribal communities to manage common resources (forests, water reservoirs) in ways acceptable to them. Gives more powers to Gram Sabhas in these areas. Elected panchayats must get Gram Sabha consent. Balances modern elected bodies with local traditions of self-government.

nodes.label: Disintegration of the USSR
nodes.detail: In December 1991, Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus declared the Soviet Union disbanded under Yeltsin's leadership. Communist Party was banned. Caused by economic stagnation, Gorbachev's reforms, nationalist movements in republics, and the failed 1991 coup.

nodes.label: Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)
nodes.detail: Formed in December 1991 after the USSR's dissolution by Russia, Ukraine, and Belarus. Central Asian republics were later made founding members. Russia accepted as successor state of the USSR, inheriting the UN Security Council seat.

nodes.label: Shock Therapy
nodes.detail: Model of transition from socialism to capitalism in post-Soviet states, influenced by World Bank and IMF. Involved rapid privatisation, free trade, currency convertibility, and FDI. Led to economic ruin, massive inequality, rise of mafia, collapse of industries, and loss of social welfare.

nodes.label: India-Russia Relations
nodes.detail: Built on Cold War-era trust. Over 80 bilateral agreements under the Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement of 2001. Russia is India's major arms supplier and supports India on Kashmir. Cooperation in energy, space technology, and nuclear energy. Both advocate multipolar world order.

nodes.label: Yugoslav Breakup and Balkan Conflicts
nodes.detail: After 1991, Yugoslavia broke apart with Croatia, Slovenia, and Bosnia declaring independence. Ethnic Serbs opposed this, leading to massacres of non-Serb Bosnians. NATO intervened with bombing of Yugoslavia. Most severe post-Cold War European conflict.

nodes.label: First Gulf War (Operation Desert Storm)
nodes.detail: In 1990, Iraq invaded Kuwait. A UN-mandated coalition of 660,000 troops from 34 countries, led by the US (75% of forces), defeated Iraq in 1991. Revealed the vast technological gap in US military capability. Called a 'computer war' for use of smart bombs.

nodes.label: 9/11 Attacks
nodes.detail: On 11 September 2001, 19 hijackers flew planes into the World Trade Centre in New York and the Pentagon. Nearly 3,000 killed. Most severe attack on US soil since 1776. Led to the Global War on Terror, invasion of Afghanistan and Iraq.

nodes.label: Global War on Terror
nodes.detail: US response to 9/11 under President George W. Bush. Included Operation Enduring Freedom against Al-Qaeda and Taliban in Afghanistan, secret prisons, Guantanamo Bay detentions, and the Iraq invasion. Bypassed international law and UN provisions.

nodes.label: Iraq Invasion (Operation Iraqi Freedom)
nodes.detail: US invaded Iraq on 19 March 2003 with a coalition of the willing after UN refused mandate. Ostensible reason was preventing WMDs, but none were found. Saddam Hussein's government fell swiftly, but a full insurgency followed. Widely seen as a military and political failure.

nodes.label: Al-Qaeda
nodes.detail: Terrorist organisation influenced by extremist Islamist ideas. Bombed US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania in 1998. Carried out 9/11 attacks. Led by Osama bin Laden. US launched operations against Al-Qaeda in Sudan, Afghanistan, and globally.

nodes.label: Taliban
nodes.detail: Islamic fundamentalist regime in Afghanistan that harboured Al-Qaeda. Overthrown by US-led Operation Enduring Freedom after 9/11. Remnants continued as potent force launching terrorist attacks against Western targets.

nodes.label: India-US Relations
nodes.detail: India was on the opposite side during the Cold War but relations improved after 1991 economic liberalisation. New factors: technology sector (65% of India's software exports to US, 35% of Boeing's technical staff of Indian origin) and the Indian-American diaspora. Three strategic options debated in India.

nodes.label: Clinton Presidency
nodes.detail: Bill Clinton was US President 1993-2001. Focused on soft issues: democracy promotion, climate change, world trade. Used military force in Kosovo (1999 NATO bombing of Yugoslavia) and against Al-Qaeda in Sudan and Afghanistan (Operation Infinite Reach 1998).

nodes.label: European Union (EU)
nodes.detail: Established in 1992 by Treaty of Maastricht. Evolved from EEC (1957). World's biggest economy (GDP over $12 trillion in 2005). Has its own flag, anthem, currency (euro), common foreign and security policy. Two members (UK, France) hold UNSC permanent seats. Combined armed forces second largest globally.

nodes.label: ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF)
nodes.detail: Established in 1994. Coordinates security and foreign policy for ASEAN. Only regional association in Asia providing a political forum where Asian countries and major powers discuss security concerns.

nodes.label: India's Look East Policy
nodes.detail: India's policy since 1991 to strengthen ties with ASEAN and East Asian nations. India signed FTAs with Singapore and Thailand. Seeks FTA with ASEAN itself. Led to greater economic interaction with ASEAN, China, Japan, and South Korea.

nodes.label: Treaty of Maastricht
nodes.detail: Signed on 7 February 1992, establishing the European Union. Laid foundation for common foreign and security policy, cooperation on justice and home affairs, and creation of single currency. Denmark and Sweden resisted some provisions.

nodes.label: Nuclear Tests 1998
nodes.detail: India conducted nuclear tests at Pokhran in May 1998 (first test was in 1974). Pakistan responded within days with tests at Chagai Hills. Both states became declared nuclear powers. Changed the military relationship with possibility of direct full-scale war declining.

nodes.label: South Asian Free Trade Agreement (SAFTA)
nodes.detail: Signed at the 12th SAARC Summit in Islamabad in 2004, effective from January 2006. Aims to lower trade tariffs by 20% by 2007. Smaller neighbours fear Indian market domination. India argues economic benefits for all from freer trade.

nodes.label: India-Nepal Relations
nodes.detail: Special relationship allowing citizens to travel and work without visas. Disputes over trade, Nepal's ties with China, and Indian interference. India concerned about Maoist movement spreading. Relations held together by trade, electricity cooperation, and water management.

nodes.label: India's UNSC Permanent Membership Bid
nodes.detail: India argues for permanent membership based on: second most populous country, largest democracy, participated in virtually all UN initiatives, long peacekeeping record, growing economic power, regular financial contributor. Opposed by Pakistan and some others over nuclear weapons and regional conflicts.

nodes.label: Chemical Weapons Convention (CWC)
nodes.detail: Signed in 1992. Banned the production and possession of chemical weapons. 181 states acceded. Included all great powers. India is a signatory. Frequently tested in UPSC.

nodes.label: Earth Summit (Rio 1992)
nodes.detail: UN Conference on Environment and Development held in Rio de Janeiro, June 1992. Attended by 170 states, thousands of NGOs, and MNCs. Produced conventions on climate change, biodiversity, forestry, and Agenda 21. Established principle of common but differentiated responsibilities.

nodes.label: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)
nodes.detail: 1992 convention providing that parties should act on basis of equity and common but differentiated responsibilities. Acknowledged that largest share of historical greenhouse gas emissions originated in developed countries. Per capita emissions in developing countries still relatively low.

nodes.label: Kyoto Protocol
nodes.detail: 1997 international agreement setting targets for industrialised countries to cut greenhouse gas emissions (CO2, methane, hydrofluorocarbons). Based on UNFCCC principles. India and China exempted. India signed and ratified in August 2002. Some major countries did not sign.

nodes.label: India's Stand on Environmental Issues
nodes.detail: Signed and ratified Kyoto Protocol in 2002. Position based on historical responsibility principle from UNFCCC. Per capita emissions far below world average (0.9 tonnes in 2000 vs 3.8 world average). National Auto-fuel Policy, Energy Conservation Act 2001, Electricity Act 2003, renewable energy programmes.

nodes.label: India and Globalisation
nodes.detail: After independence, India adopted protectionism. In 1991, responding to financial crisis, India embarked on economic reforms including de-regulation of trade and foreign investment. Previously sluggish growth rate improved. Challenge is ensuring benefits of growth are shared.

nodes.label: WTO Seattle Protests (1999)
nodes.detail: Widespread protests at the 1999 WTO Ministerial Meeting in Seattle alleging unfair trading practices by economically powerful states. Argued that developing world interests were insufficiently represented in evolving global economic system.

nodes.label: World Social Forum (WSF)
nodes.detail: Global platform bringing together human rights activists, environmentalists, labour, youth, and women activists opposed to neo-liberal globalisation. First meeting in Porto Alegre, Brazil in 2001. Fourth meeting in Mumbai 2004. Seventh in Nairobi, Kenya 2007.

nodes.label: Kargil Conflict (1999)
nodes.detail: In early 1999, forces claiming to be Mujahideens occupied Indian positions along the LoC in Kargil sector. India recovered control by 26 July 1999. Significant because both India and Pakistan had attained nuclear capability in 1998. Led to the fall of PM Nawaz Sharif's government in Pakistan.

nodes.label: Anti-Arrack Movement
nodes.detail: Spontaneous mobilisation of rural women in Andhra Pradesh in 1992 demanding ban on sale of arrack (locally brewed alcohol). Started in Nellore district through adult literacy classes. Women of about 5000 villages passed prohibition resolutions. Connected to broader issues of domestic violence, rural indebtedness and criminalisation of politics.

nodes.label: National Fish Workers Forum (NFF)
nodes.detail: Platform for fishworkers formed to fight against mechanised trawlers and bottom trawling threatening traditional livelihoods. In 1991, successfully fought a legal battle against the government's deep sea fishing policy that opened India's waters to multinational companies. Called nationwide strike in 2002.

nodes.label: Babri Masjid Demolition (1992)
nodes.detail: On 6 December 1992, thousands gathered at Ayodhya and demolished the 16th century Babri Masjid despite Supreme Court orders. Triggered Hindu-Muslim clashes across the country. BJP-ruled state governments dismissed. BJP expressed regret. Raised fundamental questions about secularism and Indian nationalism.

nodes.label: New Economic Policy / LPG Reforms
nodes.detail: Structural adjustment programme initiated by Rajiv Gandhi and made visible in 1991 under PM Narasimha Rao and FM Manmohan Singh. Marked Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation. Radically changed India's economic direction from the Nehruvian mixed economy model. Widely criticised by movements and organisations but continued by all governments.

nodes.label: Assassination of Rajiv Gandhi (1991)
nodes.detail: PM Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated in May 1991 by a Sri Lankan Tamil linked to the LTTE during an election campaign in Tamil Nadu. Led to change in Congress leadership. Narasimha Rao became PM. Congress won 1991 elections as the single largest party.

nodes.label: Gujarat Violence (2002)
nodes.detail: In February-March 2002, large-scale violence against Muslims in Gujarat after Godhra train burning incident (57 karsevaks killed). Nearly 1100 persons, mostly Muslims, killed. NHRC criticised Gujarat government. Election Commission postponed assembly elections. PM Vajpayee urged Gujarat CM to follow 'raj dharma'.

nodes.label: African National Congress
nodes.detail: A group of people who led the struggle against apartheid in South Africa. Along with Nelson Mandela, the ANC fought for racial equality and eventually succeeded in establishing democracy in South Africa in 1994.
nodes.chapter_title: Key Elements of a Democratic Government

nodes.label: Surat Plague Scare 1994
nodes.detail: In 1994, Surat had a plague scare due to being one of the dirtiest cities in India. Houses and restaurants dumped garbage into drains and streets, and the Municipal Corporation failed in garbage collection. Several people died and over 300,000 fled. After this, Surat became one of the cleanest cities.

nodes.label: Swachh Bharat Mission
nodes.detail: Launched by the Government of India on 2 October 2014 to promote cleanliness in both rural and urban areas. Includes the Swachh Bharat Swachh Vidyalaya campaign for sanitation awareness in schools. Implemented by municipalities and panchayats.

nodes.label: Mid-Day Meal Scheme
nodes.detail: Government programme providing cooked lunch in all government elementary schools. Tamil Nadu was the first state to introduce it. In 2001, the Supreme Court directed all states to implement it within six months. It improved school enrollment, attendance, and helped reduce caste prejudices.

nodes.label: Government Programmes for Equality
nodes.detail: The government implements equality through two methods: laws that protect equal treatment, and schemes or programmes to help disadvantaged communities gain greater opportunities. These target communities treated unequally for centuries.

nodes.label: Hakim Seikh Case
nodes.detail: Hakim Seikh, an agricultural labourer in West Bengal, was denied treatment at eight government hospitals after a train accident in 1992. The court ruled the government must provide emergency medical treatment and that denial violates the Right to Life. State was ordered to reimburse his expenses.
nodes.chapter_title: Role of the Government in Health

nodes.label: Kerala Health Model
nodes.detail: In 1996, the Kerala government allocated 40 percent of the state budget to panchayats for local planning of water, food, education, and health. This decentralised approach improved health centres, school functioning, and water supply schemes.
nodes.chapter_title: Role of the Government in Health

nodes.label: Campaign Against Dowry Deaths
nodes.detail: In the 1980s, womens groups across India spoke out against cases of young brides being murdered by in-laws or husbands for more dowry. Through street protests, court approaches, and information sharing, they made it a public issue and dowry laws were strengthened.

nodes.label: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act 2005
nodes.detail: Law made in 2006 (enacted 2005) to give women who face physical and mental violence within their homes legal protection. A key achievement of the womens movement in getting legislation to address violence within the private sphere of the family.

nodes.label: Supreme Court Guidelines on Sexual Harassment
nodes.detail: In 1997, the Supreme Court formulated guidelines (Vishaka guidelines) to protect women against sexual harassment at the workplace and within educational institutions. This was a result of efforts by the womens movement and was later codified into law.

nodes.label: Beti Bachao Beti Padhao
nodes.detail: Campaign launched in 2014 to address declining child sex ratio and promote education of the girl child. Represents government recognition that gender equality requires both protection and empowerment of women through education.

nodes.label: Tawa Matsya Sangh (TMS)
nodes.detail: Federation of fisherworker cooperatives in Madhya Pradesh fighting for rights of displaced forest dwellers of Satpura forest. After Tawa dam displaced them, government gave fishing rights to private contractors. TMS organised protests and in 1996 won fishing rights. Members now earn three times more through cooperative marketing.

nodes.label: Sachar Committee Report
nodes.detail: A high-level committee chaired by Justice Rajindar Sachar set up in 2005 to examine social, economic, and educational status of Muslims. Found Muslim community's situation comparable to SCs and STs on many indicators. Debunked myths like preference for madrasas (only 4% attend). Average years of schooling for Muslim children much lower.

nodes.label: Niyamgiri Hill - Adivasi Resistance
nodes.detail: Niyamgiri in Kalahandi, Odisha, is the sacred mountain of Dongarria Konds (Adivasi community). A major aluminium company planned a mine and refinery here, threatening displacement. The community strongly resisted, joined by environmentalists. A case was pending in the Supreme Court.

nodes.label: SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
nodes.detail: Framed in response to demands by Dalits for government action against everyday ill-treatment and violence. Lists various levels of crimes: physical humiliation, dispossession of resources, forced slave labour, and crimes against Dalit/tribal women. Prescribes stringent punishments. Also used by Adivasis to defend land rights.

nodes.label: Manual Scavengers Prohibition Act 1993
nodes.detail: Prohibited employment of manual scavengers and construction of dry latrines. Despite the law, manual scavenging persisted. Safai Karamchari Andolan filed PIL in Supreme Court in 2003. The 2013 Act replaced it with stronger provisions for prohibition and rehabilitation.

nodes.label: Forest Rights Act 2006
nodes.detail: The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006. Meant to undo historical injustices to forest-dwelling populations. Recognises rights to homestead, cultivable and grazing land, and non-timber forest produce. Also recognises forest dwellers' role in conservation.

nodes.label: Safai Karamchari Andolan
nodes.detail: An Andhra Pradesh-based organisation working with manual scavengers. Filed PIL in Supreme Court in 2003 with 13 other organisations and 7 scavengers. Complained that manual scavenging persisted despite 1993 Act. Supreme Court directed governments to verify and take time-bound rehabilitation action.

nodes.label: Environmental Protection Laws
nodes.detail: After Bhopal, India introduced new environmental laws. The polluter is held accountable for environmental damage. In Subhash Kumar vs State of Bihar (1991), Supreme Court held Right to Life includes right to pollution-free water and air. Government must check pollution, clean rivers, and impose heavy fines.

nodes.label: Child Labour Laws
nodes.detail: The Child Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986, amended in 2016, bans employment of children below 14 in all occupations and adolescents (14-18) in hazardous work. Violation is a cognizable offence with jail term of 6 months to 2 years and/or fine of Rs 20,000-50,000. PENCIL portal launched in 2017.

nodes.label: CNG Order by Supreme Court
nodes.detail: In a series of rulings from 1998 onwards, the Supreme Court ordered all public transport vehicles using diesel in Delhi to switch to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG). This significantly reduced air pollution. But diesel cars and increased vehicle numbers continued to cause pollution concerns.

nodes.label: End of Cold War and Democracy
nodes.detail: Collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991 led to democratisation in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Many former communist countries transitioned to multi-party democracies. Democracy became the dominant form globally.

nodes.label: Pakistan under Musharraf
nodes.detail: General Pervez Musharraf led military coup in October 1999. Amended constitution via Legal Framework Order (2002) giving President power to dismiss assemblies. National Security Council dominated by military. Elections held but real power with army, not elected reps.

nodes.label: China's Single Party System
nodes.detail: China holds elections every five years for National People's Congress (nearly 3,000 members). But candidates need Communist Party approval. Only CCP and eight allied parties allowed. Government always formed by Communist Party. Not a democracy by any definition.

nodes.label: Zimbabwe under Mugabe
nodes.detail: Robert Mugabe ruled since independence in 1980. Won elections but used unfair practices. Changed constitution to increase presidential powers. Opposition harassed, protests declared illegal, press freedom curtailed, judiciary pressurised. Forced out in 2017.

nodes.label: South African Constitution
nodes.detail: Drafted after two years of negotiations between oppressor and oppressed groups. Gave citizens most extensive rights available. Based on principles of equality, democratic values, social justice and human rights. Model for democracies worldwide.

nodes.label: LPG Reforms (July 1991)
nodes.detail: Liberalisation + Privatisation + Globalisation reforms launched 24 July 1991 by FM Manmohan Singh under PM Narasimha Rao. Triggered by BOP crisis (forex <15 days imports) + IMF conditionality. Rupee devalued 2x (July 1-3). Industrial Policy 24 July abolished licence raj for most industries. FERA liberalised. Landmark moment ending Nehruvian planning era.

nodes.label: Manmohan Singh (FM 1991-96)
nodes.detail: Finance Minister 21 June 1991 - 16 May 1996 under Narasimha Rao. Architect of 1991 reforms budget (24 July 1991). Earlier: Economic Advisor, RBI Governor 1982-85, Planning Commission. PM 2004-2014. Delivered 'No power on earth can stop an idea whose time has come'.

nodes.label: NREGA 2005 (Right to Work)
nodes.detail: National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005. Guarantees 100 days of employment per year to those able and in need. Government must provide unemployment allowance if it fails. Preference for work that increases future land productivity. Initially covered 200 districts.

nodes.label: Liberalisation
nodes.detail: Removing barriers or restrictions set by government on foreign trade and investment. India began liberalising around 1991 -- allowing freer imports, exports, and foreign companies to set up operations. Post-independence, India had protective trade barriers for domestic producers. Decision supported by powerful international organisations.

nodes.label: 1991 Economic Reforms
nodes.detail: Far-reaching policy changes in India around 1991. Government decided Indian producers should compete globally. Barriers on foreign trade and investment were significantly removed. Goods could be imported and exported more freely. Foreign companies allowed to set up factories and offices in India.

nodes.label: Right to Information Act (RTI), 2005
nodes.detail: Enacted October 2005 by Government of India. Ensures citizens can access information about functions of government departments. Expands the right to information beyond consumer goods to government services. Empowers citizens to question government and seek accountability.

nodes.label: Balance of Payments Crisis 1991
nodes.detail: India faced an external debt crisis -- government could not repay foreign borrowings, forex reserves fell to less than two weeks of imports. Rising prices of essential goods compounded the crisis. Root cause: inefficient economic management in the 1980s with expenditure exceeding revenue, profligate spending of borrowed forex on consumption.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: New Economic Policy (NEP) 1991
nodes.detail: Wide-ranging reforms announced after India received $7 billion loan from World Bank and IMF. Consisted of stabilisation measures (short-term: forex reserves, inflation control) and structural reforms (long-term: efficiency, international competitiveness). Three pillars: Liberalisation, Privatisation, and Globalisation.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Deregulation of Industrial Sector
nodes.detail: Industrial licensing abolished for almost all products except alcohol, cigarettes, hazardous chemicals, industrial explosives, electronics, aerospace, and drugs/pharmaceuticals. Only defence equipment, atomic energy, and railway transport reserved for public sector. Small-scale industry reservations were dereserved. Market-determined pricing allowed.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Financial Sector Reforms
nodes.detail: Aimed at reducing RBI's role from regulator to facilitator. Private sector banks (Indian and foreign) allowed. Foreign investment limit in banks raised to 50%. Banks given freedom to set up branches without RBI approval. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) including merchant bankers, mutual funds, pension funds allowed to invest.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Tax Reforms Post-1991
nodes.detail: Continuous reduction in income tax rates to encourage savings and voluntary disclosure (high rates had caused evasion). Corporation tax gradually reduced. Indirect taxes reformed to facilitate a common national market. Procedures simplified and rates substantially lowered for better compliance.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Foreign Exchange Reforms
nodes.detail: Rupee was devalued against foreign currencies in 1991 as immediate crisis measure, increasing foreign exchange inflow. Market-determined exchange rates replaced government-controlled rates. This freed the determination of rupee value based on demand and supply of foreign exchange.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Trade and Investment Policy Reforms
nodes.detail: Dismantling of quantitative restrictions on imports and exports, reduction of tariff rates, removal of import licensing (except hazardous/environmentally sensitive industries). Quantitative restrictions on manufactured consumer goods and agricultural products fully removed from April 2001. Export duties removed for international competitiveness.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Privatisation
nodes.detail: Shedding of government ownership or management of enterprises. Two methods: withdrawal from ownership/management, or outright sale. Purpose: improve financial discipline, facilitate modernisation, attract FDI, and utilise private capital and managerial capabilities. Some PSUs given autonomy as Navaratnas and Miniratnas instead of being sold.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Disinvestment
nodes.detail: Selling off part of equity of Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) to the public. Critics argue PSU assets were undervalued and sold cheaply. Proceeds were used to offset revenue shortfalls rather than developing PSUs or building social infrastructure. Annual targets set by government, sometimes exceeded.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Navaratna PSUs
nodes.detail: In 1996, nine PSUs were given greater managerial and operational autonomy to improve efficiency and compete globally. Original nine included IOC, BPCL, HPCL, ONGC, SAIL, IPCL, BHEL, NTPC, VSNL. Later GAIL and MTNL added. Also 97 profit-making PSUs designated as Miniratnas. Better performance resulted from this status.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Stabilisation Measures
nodes.detail: Short-term measures to correct weaknesses in balance of payments and control inflation. Included maintaining sufficient foreign exchange reserves and controlling rising prices. Part of the NEP alongside long-term structural reforms.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Structural Reform Measures
nodes.detail: Long-term measures to improve efficiency and increase international competitiveness by removing rigidities in the economy. Encompassed liberalisation (industrial, financial, trade), privatisation, and policies that led to globalisation. Aimed at creating a more competitive economic environment.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: Rupee Devaluation 1991
nodes.detail: As an immediate measure to resolve the balance of payments crisis, the rupee was devalued against foreign currencies in 1991. This increased inflow of foreign exchange and set the tone for market-determined exchange rates, moving away from government-controlled currency valuation.
nodes.chapter_title: Liberalisation, Privatisation and Globalisation: An Appraisal

nodes.label: 86th Constitutional Amendment (Right to Education)
nodes.detail: In December 2002, made free and compulsory education a fundamental right for all children aged 6-14 years. The Constitution's Directive Principles originally set a target of achieving this within 10 years (by 1960). Tapas Majumdar Committee (1998) estimated Rs 1.37 lakh crore needed over 10 years to achieve this.

nodes.label: Golden Revolution (Horticulture)
nodes.detail: Period 1991-2003 called Golden Revolution when planned investment in horticulture became highly productive. India emerged as world leader in mangoes, bananas, coconuts, cashew nuts, and spices; second largest producer of fruits and vegetables. Provides employment to 19% of total labour force. Flower harvesting and food processing are remunerative for rural women.

nodes.label: Kudumbashree
nodes.detail: Women-oriented community-based poverty reduction programme in Kerala. Started in 1995 as thrift and credit society for poor women. Mobilised Rs 1 crore as thrift savings. Acclaimed as the largest informal bank in Asia in terms of participation and savings mobilised. Functions like mini banks through micro-credit system.

nodes.label: Inflation Targeting
nodes.detail: A monetary policy framework where the central bank commits to keeping inflation at a specified target. In India, the inflation target is 4% CPI with a tolerance band of +/- 2% (2-6%). RBI uses CPI (not WPI) as the key measure for inflation targeting since 2016. If inflation exceeds 6% for three consecutive quarters, MPC must explain to the government.

nodes.label: Goods and Services Tax (GST)
nodes.detail: A comprehensive indirect tax on manufacture, sale, and consumption of goods and services. Replaced multiple taxes to create a single national market. Dual GST model: CGST (Centre) + SGST (State) for intra-state; IGST for inter-state. Implemented from July 1, 2017 via 101st Constitutional Amendment. GST Council determines rates.
nodes.chapter_title: The Government Budget and the Economy

nodes.label: Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management Act (FRBMA)
nodes.detail: Enacted in 2003 to institutionalize fiscal discipline. Targets: elimination of revenue deficit and reduction of fiscal deficit. Mandates the Finance Minister to present the Macro Economic Framework Statement before Parliament. Restricts RBI from buying government securities in primary market (no monetization). FRBM Review Committee recommended 60% debt-to-GDP ratio.
nodes.chapter_title: The Government Budget and the Economy

nodes.label: MGNREGA (2005)
nodes.detail: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act guarantees 100 days of wage employment per household per year. Aims at livelihood security in rural areas and sustainable development. One-third jobs reserved for women. Provided employment to 4.78 crore households.

nodes.label: Prime Minister Rozgar Yojana (PMRY)
nodes.detail: Started in 1993 to create self-employment opportunities for educated unemployed youth in rural areas and small towns. Helps in setting up small business and industries.

nodes.label: Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY)
nodes.detail: Launched in 1999 to bring assisted poor families above the poverty line by organising them into self-help groups (SHGs). Uses a mix of bank credit and government subsidy for self-employment generation.

nodes.label: Antyodaya Anna Yojana (AAY)
nodes.detail: Launched December 2000 for the poorest among BPL families. Initially 1 crore families, expanded to 2 crore. Provides 35 kg of foodgrains at Rs 2/kg (wheat) and Rs 3/kg (rice). Identified through BPL surveys by state rural development departments.

nodes.label: Spreading Production Across Countries
nodes.detail: MNCs divide production into small parts spread globally. Example: design in US, components in China, assembly in Mexico/Eastern Europe, customer care in India -- saving 50-60% costs. Methods: joint ventures with local companies, using local suppliers, buying local companies, placing orders with small producers.

nodes.label: 1989 General Elections
nodes.detail: Ninth Lok Sabha elections, December 1989. Congress reduced from 415 (1984) to 197 seats — end of the 'Congress system'. Coalition era begins. National Front (Janata Dal + regional parties) formed government under V.P. Singh, supported by BJP and Left Front from outside.

nodes.label: V.P. Singh (PM 1989-90)
nodes.detail: Prime Minister, December 1989 to November 1990. Led National Front government. Implemented Mandal Commission recommendations in August 1990. Government fell after BJP withdrew support over Advani's Rath Yatra arrest.

nodes.label: National Front Government (1989-90)
nodes.detail: Coalition government under V.P. Singh, 1989-90. Alliance of Janata Dal + regional parties. Supported from outside by BJP (right) and Left Front. First major non-Congress non-emergency coalition era government.

nodes.label: Shah Bano Case (1985)
nodes.detail: 62-year-old divorced Muslim woman sought maintenance from former husband. Supreme Court (1985) ruled in her favour under Section 125 CrPC. Orthodox Muslims protested judicial 'interference' in Personal Law. Rajiv Gandhi government passed Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986 to override the ruling. Fueled BJP critique of 'appeasement' and Hindutva rise.

nodes.label: Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act 1986
nodes.detail: Passed by Rajiv Gandhi government to nullify the Shah Bano Supreme Court judgment. Made Muslim personal law applicable to maintenance disputes between divorced Muslim couples. Widely criticised as minority 'appeasement'. Basis for BJP's critique of pseudo-secularism.

nodes.label: Mandal Commission (1978-80)
nodes.detail: Second Backward Classes Commission, chaired by B.P. Mandal. Set up 1978 by Janata government, submitted report 1980. Recommended 27% reservation for OBCs in central government jobs and educational institutions, based on caste-based social and educational backwardness. Report shelved until 1990.

nodes.label: Mandal Implementation (August 1990)
nodes.detail: V.P. Singh government decided in August 1990 to implement Mandal Commission's 27% OBC reservation in central government jobs and PSUs. Triggered violent anti-Mandal agitations in North India — students self-immolated. Reshaped politics around caste mobilisation.

nodes.label: Indra Sawhney Case (Mandal, 1992)
nodes.detail: Supreme Court 9-judge bench (1992) upheld 27% OBC reservation but capped total reservation at 50%. Introduced 'creamy layer' exclusion from OBC benefits. Held that reservation in promotions not permissible. Foundational case for reservation jurisprudence.

nodes.label: Advani's Rath Yatra (1990)
nodes.detail: L.K. Advani led a 10,000-km Rath Yatra from Somnath (Gujarat) to Ayodhya in September-October 1990 to mobilise Hindus for Ram Janmabhoomi temple construction. Advani arrested in Bihar by CM Lalu Yadav. BJP withdrew support from V.P. Singh government, causing its fall.

nodes.label: Chandra Shekhar (PM 1990-91)
nodes.detail: Prime Minister, 10 November 1990 to 21 June 1991. Led breakaway Samajwadi Janata Party with Congress external support. Handled the 1991 BoP crisis, pledging gold to IMF. Resigned when Congress withdrew support in March 1991.

nodes.label: Anti-Sikh Riots (November 1984)
nodes.detail: Mass communal violence against Sikhs following Indira Gandhi's assassination (31 October 1984). ~3,000 Sikhs killed, mostly in Delhi. Nanavati Commission (2005) indicted several Congress leaders. Chronic impunity issue for Indian secularism.

nodes.label: 1993 Mumbai Serial Blasts (12 March 1993)
nodes.detail: Thirteen coordinated bomb blasts in Mumbai, 12 March 1993; killed 257 and injured 713. Retaliation for Babri demolition and communal riots. Planned by Dawood Ibrahim's D-Company with ISI facilitation. Yakub Memon hanged 2015.

nodes.label: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP, 1980)
nodes.detail: Political party formed 6 April 1980 by former Jana Sangh members after Janata Party split. Initially adopted 'Gandhian Socialism'; shifted to Hindutva from mid-1980s under Advani. Rose via Ram Janmabhoomi movement (1989 → 85 MPs; 1991 → 120; 1996 → 161 largest).

nodes.label: Hindutva Politics
nodes.detail: Political ideology defined by V.D. Savarkar (1923) as the basis of Indian nationhood — acceptance of India as pitrubhu (fatherland) and punyabhu (holy land). Adopted by BJP from mid-1980s as mobilising strategy. Became central to BJP's electoral rise via Ram Janmabhoomi movement.

nodes.label: Ayodhya Dispute — Faizabad Court Unlocking (February 1986)
nodes.detail: Faizabad district court ordered Babri Masjid premises unlocked in February 1986 for Hindu darshan. Triggered mobilisation by VHP/RSS/BJP around Ram Janmabhoomi claim and counter-mobilisation by Muslim organisations. Converted local dispute into national communal flashpoint.

nodes.label: Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP)
nodes.detail: Hindu nationalist organisation formed 1964, became prominent in Ram Janmabhoomi agitation 1984 onwards. Spearheaded shila pujan (1989), kar seva programmes. Part of RSS-led Sangh Parivar along with BJP, Bajrang Dal, ABVP.

nodes.label: Godhra Train Burning (27 February 2002)
nodes.detail: Coach S-6 of Sabarmati Express set on fire at Godhra railway station, 27 February 2002; 59 kar sevaks returning from Ayodhya killed. Triggered large-scale Gujarat riots. SIT investigation (2011) convicted 31 people; Gujarat HC upheld 11 death sentences (commuted to life by SC in 2017).

nodes.label: Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP, 1984)
nodes.detail: Political party founded 14 April 1984 by Kanshi Ram, representing Bahujans (SC/ST/OBC/minorities). Major force in UP from 1990s. Mayawati CM four times (1995, 1997, 2002-03, 2007-12). Peaked 2007 with absolute majority in UP.

nodes.label: Kanshi Ram (1934-2006)
nodes.detail: Dalit politician, founder of BAMCEF (1978), DS-4 (1981), and Bahujan Samaj Party (1984). Mentor of Mayawati. Credited with Dalit political mobilisation in North India. Advocated 'Bahujan' coalition of SC/ST/OBC/minorities.

nodes.label: United Front Government (1996-98)
nodes.detail: Coalition of 13 parties (Janata Dal, DMK, Samajwadi Party, TDP, AGP, Left Front) that governed 1996-98 with Congress external support. Two PMs: H.D. Deve Gowda (June 1996 - April 1997) and I.K. Gujral (April 1997 - March 1998). Congress withdrew support over CBI investigation of DMK.

nodes.label: H.D. Deve Gowda (PM 1996-97)
nodes.detail: Prime Minister, 1 June 1996 to 21 April 1997. Janata Dal leader, former Karnataka CM. Led United Front coalition with Congress outside support. Replaced by Gujral after Congress demanded leadership change.

nodes.label: I.K. Gujral (PM 1997-98)
nodes.detail: Prime Minister, 21 April 1997 to 19 March 1998. Janata Dal leader, former External Affairs Minister. Formulated the Gujral Doctrine of non-reciprocal concessions to South Asian neighbours. Government fell over Jain Commission report on Rajiv Gandhi assassination and DMK.

nodes.label: Gujral Doctrine (1996-97)
nodes.detail: Five-point foreign policy articulated by I.K. Gujral for India's relations with South Asian neighbours: non-reciprocal concessions to smaller neighbours, no interference in internal affairs, respect for territorial integrity, dispute resolution via peaceful bilateral negotiations, no use of territory against another South Asian country.

nodes.label: Atal Bihari Vajpayee (PM, full term 1999-2004)
nodes.detail: BJP leader, three-time PM: 13 days (May 1996), 13 months (March 1998 - April 1999), full term (October 1999 - May 2004). Led NDA government. Oversaw Pokhran-II (1998), Kargil War (1999), Lahore Bus Yatra, Golden Quadrilateral, SSA, Privatisation push.

nodes.label: National Democratic Alliance (NDA, 1998)
nodes.detail: BJP-led coalition formed 1998. Initial constituents: BJP, Shiv Sena, Samata Party, BJD, TDP (outside support), AIADMK (briefly). Vajpayee PM 1998-99, 1999-2004. Modi PM 2014-, 2019-, 2024-. Replaced Hindutva ideological thrust with common governance programme (National Agenda).

nodes.label: United Progressive Alliance (UPA, 2004)
nodes.detail: Congress-led coalition formed May 2004 after 2004 Lok Sabha elections. Initial constituents: Congress, DMK, NCP, RJD, JMM, LJP etc. with Left Front outside support. Manmohan Singh PM 2004-14 (UPA-I and UPA-II).

nodes.label: 2004 General Elections (UPA-I)
nodes.detail: 14th Lok Sabha elections, April-May 2004. BJP-led NDA's 'India Shining' campaign failed. Congress 145, BJP 138. UPA formed with Left support. Sonia Gandhi declined PM; Manmohan Singh sworn in 22 May 2004.

nodes.label: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC, 1993)
nodes.detail: Statutory body established under Protection of Human Rights Act 1993. Chairperson + members investigate human rights violations. Played key role criticising Gujarat 2002 riots response. Members: former CJI (chairperson), former SC/HC judges, human rights experts.

nodes.label: Industrial Policy Statement 24 July 1991
nodes.detail: New Industrial Policy announced 24 July 1991 alongside Manmohan Singh's budget. Abolished industrial licensing except for 18 industries (later reduced to 6); abolished MRTP asset threshold; allowed 51% FDI in 34 high-priority industries; ended public sector monopoly in most areas; provided for disinvestment of loss-making PSUs. End of licence raj.

nodes.label: IMF Bailout 1991 ($7bn Loan)
nodes.detail: India approached IMF/World Bank (IBRD) in 1991 during the BoP crisis, receiving ~$7 billion loan. Conditionalities required liberalisation, opening to private sector, reduced government role, trade deregulation. Accepted by Chandra Shekhar government (emergency gold pledge) and Narasimha Rao government (NEP).

nodes.label: Gold Pledge to Bank of England/Switzerland (1991)
nodes.detail: Chandra Shekhar government airlifted 46.91 tonnes of gold to Bank of England and Union Bank of Switzerland in May-June 1991 against a loan of $405 million, to meet forex obligations. Symbol of the BoP crisis depth. Repaid by November 1991.

nodes.label: Navaratnas Status (1997)
nodes.detail: Greater financial and operational autonomy granted to 9 profit-making PSUs in 1997: IOC, BPCL, HPCL, ONGC, SAIL, IPCL, BHEL, NTPC, VSNL. Later GAIL and MTNL added. Enables investments up to Rs 1,000 crore without government approval. Precursor to Maharatna scheme (2010).

nodes.label: Mini Ratnas (Category I and II)
nodes.detail: Classification of profit-making PSUs introduced 1997. Category I (Rs 300 cr pre-tax profit, 3 consecutive years) can invest up to Rs 500 cr; Category II up to Rs 300 cr. ~70 Mini Ratnas as of 2024. Provides operational autonomy to second-tier PSUs.

nodes.label: Maharatnas (2010 scheme)
nodes.detail: Top tier of PSUs with ≥Rs 5,000 cr avg annual turnover and ≥Rs 25,000 cr avg annual net worth (3 yrs). Can invest up to 15% of net worth (capped at Rs 5,000 cr) without government approval. Initial: CIL, IOC, NTPC, ONGC, SAIL; expanded to 14 including BHEL, GAIL, HPCL, BPCL, PowerGrid, HAL etc.

nodes.label: WTO Accession (1 January 1995)
nodes.detail: India joined World Trade Organisation as founding member, 1 January 1995. WTO succeeded GATT (established 1948). India committed to dismantling QRs, tariff reduction, TRIPS compliance. QRs on manufactured consumer goods and agricultural products fully removed from April 2001.

nodes.label: GATT to WTO Transition (Uruguay Round)
nodes.detail: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (1948, 23 countries) replaced by World Trade Organisation on 1 January 1995 after Uruguay Round (1986-94). Marrakesh Agreement signed 1994. WTO covers goods, services (GATS), IPR (TRIPS), dispute settlement mechanism.

nodes.label: Removal of Quantitative Restrictions (April 2001)
nodes.detail: India removed QRs on imports of all manufactured consumer goods and agricultural products from 1 April 2001, fulfilling WTO commitments. Final step of trade liberalisation started in 1991. Triggered debate on farmer competitiveness against subsidised imports.

nodes.label: Outsourcing / BPO Industry
nodes.detail: Business Process Outsourcing — Indian IT-enabled services (call centres, back-office, transcription, accounting) for developed country firms. Exploded post-2000 on low wages + skilled English-speaking manpower + telecom revolution. India became global BPO hub by mid-2000s.

nodes.label: Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs, 1992)
nodes.detail: FII investment in Indian financial markets permitted from 1992 under SEBI regulations. Merchant bankers, mutual funds, pension funds allowed to invest in Indian equity and debt. Triggered sustained portfolio flows; today FPIs hold ~16% of Indian equity market.

nodes.label: Special Economic Zones (SEZ) Act 2005
nodes.detail: SEZ Act passed 2005, operational April 2006. Duty-free enclaves with simplified procedures, tax holidays, single-window clearances to attract FDI and boost exports. Controversial over land acquisition (Nandigram, Singur, POSCO protests). 378+ approved SEZs as of 2024.

nodes.label: Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA) 1999
nodes.detail: Passed 1999, operational 1 June 2000. Replaced draconian Foreign Exchange Regulation Act (FERA) 1973. Facilitated external trade and payments, promoted orderly forex market development. Civil rather than criminal offences. RBI as regulator.

nodes.label: Fall of the Berlin Wall (9 November 1989)
nodes.detail: Berlin Wall (built 1961) opened 9 November 1989 after East German government announced free travel to West Germany. Symbolic end of Cold War and division of Europe. Led to German reunification (3 October 1990) and collapse of communist regimes in Eastern Europe.

nodes.label: Soviet Union Disintegration (December 1991)
nodes.detail: USSR dissolved 26 December 1991. Gorbachev resigned 25 December. Triggered by nationalist movements in Baltic states (1988-90), August 1991 coup attempt against Gorbachev by hardliners, and Belavezha Accords (8 Dec 1991) signed by Russia/Ukraine/Belarus. 15 successor states formed.

nodes.label: Gorbachev's Perestroika & Glasnost (1985-91)
nodes.detail: Mikhail Gorbachev (General Secretary 1985) launched perestroika (economic restructuring) and glasnost (openness) reforms. Loosened central planning, liberalised political speech, reduced Cold War confrontation. Unintentionally triggered nationalist movements in republics; USSR collapsed 1991.

nodes.label: Boris Yeltsin (President of Russia 1991-99)
nodes.detail: First elected President of Russian Federation (1991-99). Led opposition to August 1991 coup against Gorbachev. Dissolved USSR via Belavezha Accords with Ukraine/Belarus. Oversaw shock therapy transition. Resigned 31 December 1999, handed over to Putin.

nodes.label: Indo-Russian Strategic Agreement (October 2001)
nodes.detail: Declaration on Strategic Partnership signed by PM Vajpayee and President Putin in Delhi, 4 October 2000 (not 2001 as sometimes cited). Over 80 bilateral agreements under this framework. Areas: defence, nuclear energy, space, counter-terrorism, shared vision of multipolar world.

nodes.label: George W. Bush (US President 2001-09)
nodes.detail: 43rd US President (20 January 2001 - 20 January 2009). Launched War on Terror post-9/11: Afghanistan (Oct 2001) and Iraq (March 2003). Signed Indo-US Nuclear Deal (2008). NDA relations with India deepened under his tenure — Bush/Vajpayee/Manmohan Singh era.

nodes.label: George H.W. Bush (US President 1989-93)
nodes.detail: 41st US President (January 1989 - January 1993). Presided over end of Cold War, German reunification, First Gulf War (Operation Desert Storm, 1991). Lost 1992 election to Clinton amid recession.

nodes.label: Operation Enduring Freedom (Afghanistan, Oct 2001)
nodes.detail: US-led military campaign in Afghanistan launched 7 October 2001 in response to 9/11. Toppled Taliban regime by December 2001; Hamid Karzai became interim leader. Transitioned to NATO-led ISAF (2003). US withdrew August 2021, Taliban returned.

nodes.label: US Hegemony / Unipolar Moment (1991-2008)
nodes.detail: Post-Cold War period of sole US superpower status, 1991-2008. Military (all-domain dominance), economic (dollar hegemony, WTO/IMF/World Bank), structural (cultural/institutional/ideological). Challenged post-2008 by China's rise, Russia resurgence, BRICS, 2008 financial crisis.

nodes.label: Bofors Scandal (1987)
nodes.detail: Alleged kickbacks of Rs 64 crore paid by Swedish arms firm AB Bofors to Indian officials and politicians for the 1986 contract to supply 155mm howitzer guns. Triggered V.P. Singh's resignation from Rajiv Gandhi cabinet in 1987. Became central election issue in 1989. Supreme Court quashed charges in 2004; acquittals of accused.

nodes.label: Jan Morcha (People's Front, 1987)
nodes.detail: Political grouping formed 2 October 1987 by V.P. Singh, Arif Mohammad Khan, Arun Nehru, and other Congress dissidents after their expulsion/resignation from Congress. Core of the anti-Rajiv opposition. Merged with Lok Dal, Janata, Congress(S) to form Janata Dal on 11 October 1988.

nodes.label: Janata Dal Formation (11 October 1988)
nodes.detail: Janata Dal formed 11 October 1988 (J.P. Narayan's birthday) by merging Jan Morcha, Lok Dal, Janata Party, and Congress(S). V.P. Singh elected president. Became principal non-Congress opposition party. Led the National Front in 1989 and United Front in 1996-98.

nodes.label: Allahabad By-election (June 1988)
nodes.detail: V.P. Singh won the Allahabad Lok Sabha by-election in June 1988 against Congress with Bofors gun as campaign symbol. Convinced Left and BJP that he was viable anti-Congress candidate. Led to National Front formation on 6 August 1988.

nodes.label: Kargil War (May-July 1999)
nodes.detail: Indo-Pakistani armed conflict in Kargil district of Kashmir, 3 May - 26 July 1999. Pakistan's regular army (Northern Light Infantry) and Mujahideen infiltrated across LoC and occupied heights. India launched Operation Vijay to evict them. Capture of Tololing and Tiger Hill. ~527 Indian soldiers killed. PM Vajpayee, Army Chief V.P. Malik.

nodes.label: Pokhran-II / Operation Shakti (11-13 May 1998)
nodes.detail: Five nuclear tests conducted at Pokhran range, Rajasthan, 11-13 May 1998: 3 on 11 May (one thermonuclear/hydrogen bomb, 45 kiloton yield), 2 on 13 May (sub-kiloton). PM Vajpayee declared India a nuclear weapons state. Team led by Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (DRDO) and R. Chidambaram (DAE). Triggered US/Japan/Western sanctions.

nodes.label: Lahore Bus Yatra / Lahore Declaration (February 1999)
nodes.detail: Vajpayee took inaugural Delhi-Lahore bus service on 19 February 1999. Met Pakistan PM Nawaz Sharif at Lahore. Signed Lahore Declaration 21 Feb 1999 — confidence-building measures, bilateral dispute resolution, nuclear risk reduction. Kargil War 3 months later undermined the initiative.

nodes.label: IC-814 Kandahar Hijacking (December 1999)
nodes.detail: Indian Airlines flight IC-814 (Kathmandu-Delhi) hijacked on Christmas Eve 1999 by Harkat-ul-Mujahideen. Diverted through Amritsar, Lahore, Dubai to Kandahar (Taliban-controlled). One passenger killed. Ended 31 Dec 1999 with India releasing Maulana Masood Azhar, Omar Sheikh, Mushtaq Zargar. Jaswant Singh escorted prisoners.

nodes.label: Parliament Attack (13 December 2001)
nodes.detail: Five Lashkar-e-Taiba/Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorists attacked Indian Parliament complex, 13 December 2001. 9 security personnel and a gardener killed; all 5 terrorists killed. Triggered Operation Parakram — massive 10-month Indian military mobilisation on Pakistan border. Afzal Guru hanged 2013.

nodes.label: Operation Parakram (2001-02)
nodes.detail: Largest Indian military mobilisation since 1971, launched after 13 December 2001 Parliament attack. 500,000 Indian troops deployed on Pakistan border, December 2001 to October 2002. Stood down without war but led to significant casualties via mine accidents. US/UK diplomatic pressure defused crisis.

nodes.label: Agra Summit (July 2001)
nodes.detail: Vajpayee-Musharraf summit at Agra, 14-16 July 2001. Collapsed without joint statement due to disagreement over terminology (Kashmir as 'core issue' vs 'cross-border terrorism'). Musharraf's media outreach scored PR gains. Formal resumption of dialogue delayed until SAARC Islamabad 2004.

nodes.label: Tehelka Exposé (March 2001)
nodes.detail: Online news portal Tehelka aired 'Operation West End' sting, 13 March 2001 — journalists posing as arms dealers filmed BJP president Bangaru Laxman taking Rs 1 lakh cash and Samata Party president Jaya Jaitly accepting Rs 2 lakh at Defence Minister George Fernandes's residence. Laxman and Fernandes resigned. Tehelka subsequently faced harassment.

nodes.label: 'India Shining' Campaign (2004)
nodes.detail: BJP-NDA's pre-election ad campaign, early 2004, extolling economic growth under Vajpayee. Rs 150 crore spend. Backfired — rural and poor voters felt excluded. Congress countered with 'Congress ka haath, aam aadmi ke saath'. NDA defeated in May 2004, biggest upset since 1977.

nodes.label: POTA / Prevention of Terrorism Act 2002
nodes.detail: Anti-terror law enacted 28 March 2002 replacing lapsed TADA. Passed after Parliament attack. Expanded police powers, presumption of guilt. Critics alleged misuse against minorities. Repealed in 2004 by UPA government, replaced by UAPA amendment.

nodes.label: POTA Repeal + UAPA Expansion (2004)
nodes.detail: UPA government repealed POTA in September 2004. Simultaneously amended Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA) 1967 to incorporate anti-terror provisions. UAPA further expanded 2008, 2012, 2019. Critics note UAPA more draconian than POTA in bail/evidence provisions.

nodes.label: National Advisory Council (NAC, 2004)
