nodes.label: Pratibha Patil (President 2007-12)
nodes.detail: 12th President of India (25 July 2007 - 25 July 2012). First woman President. Former Rajasthan Governor. Commuted death sentences of 35 convicts (most by any President). Approved Lokpal referral.

nodes.label: Pranab Mukherjee (President 2012-17)
nodes.detail: 13th President of India (25 July 2012 - 25 July 2017). Former Finance Minister (UPA-I and UPA-II), Congress stalwart. Known as 'the best PM India never had'. Bharat Ratna 2019. Died 31 August 2020.

nodes.label: Ram Nath Kovind (President 2017-22)
nodes.detail: 14th President of India (25 July 2017 - 25 July 2022). Second Dalit President. Former Bihar Governor. Signed Article 370 abrogation order 5 Aug 2019 and Farm Laws 2020.

nodes.label: Droupadi Murmu (President 2022-present)
nodes.detail: 15th President of India (25 July 2022 -). First tribal (Santhal) President, youngest ever (64). Former Jharkhand Governor (2015-21). Signed Women's Reservation Act 2023, new criminal laws 2023.

nodes.label: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana (PMAY, 2015)
nodes.detail: Housing for All scheme launched June 2015. PMAY-Urban (25 June) + PMAY-Gramin (November). Targets pucca houses with water/electricity/LPG/toilets. Central assistance Rs 1.2-2.5 lakh/unit. 4+ crore houses built by 2024. Target extended to 2024-29 with 3 crore more houses.

nodes.label: Smart Cities Mission (2015)
nodes.detail: Urban renewal mission launched 25 June 2015. 100 cities selected competitively. Core infrastructure + area-based development + technology solutions. Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs). Central outlay Rs 48,000 crore. Extended to March 2025 and beyond.

nodes.label: AMRUT Mission (2015)
nodes.detail: Atal Mission for Rejuvenation and Urban Transformation launched 25 June 2015. 500 cities with population >1 lakh. Water supply, sewerage, urban transport, green spaces. AMRUT 2.0 launched October 2021 for water and sewage in all urban areas.

nodes.label: Bharatmala Pariyojana (2017)
nodes.detail: Umbrella highway programme approved October 2017. Rs 5.35 lakh crore outlay (Phase I). Target 34,800 km of highways: economic corridors, inter-corridor/feeder routes, national corridors efficiency, border roads, coastal/port connectivity, expressways. Slowed rollout; partially subsumed under Gati Shakti.

nodes.label: Sagarmala Programme (2015)
nodes.detail: Port-led development programme approved March 2015. 6 Mega Ports, modernise existing ports, port-rail/road connectivity, coastal shipping, coastal community development. Aimed to reduce logistics cost for EXIM/domestic cargo. 802 projects worth Rs 5.5 lakh crore identified.

nodes.label: PM-KISAN (2018)
nodes.detail: PM Kisan Samman Nidhi launched 24 February 2019 (announced Feb 2018 Interim Budget). Rs 6,000/year DBT to all landholding farmers (earlier only small/marginal). 11+ crore beneficiaries. Rs 3.24 lakh crore disbursed by 2024 over 17 installments.

nodes.label: Saubhagya Scheme (2017)
nodes.detail: Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana, launched 25 September 2017. Universal household electrification — all remaining non-electrified rural + urban households. 2.86+ crore households electrified; India declared 100% village electrification 28 April 2018.

nodes.label: Atal Pension Yojana (APY, 2015)
nodes.detail: Pension scheme for unorganised sector workers, launched 1 June 2015 by PFRDA. Guaranteed monthly pension Rs 1,000-5,000 from age 60. Open to 18-40 years. 6+ crore subscribers by 2024. Complements NPS.

nodes.label: Vande Bharat Express Trains (2019)
nodes.detail: Indigenous semi-high-speed trains by ICF Chennai. First Vande Bharat (Delhi-Varanasi) launched 15 February 2019 by PM Modi. Integrated Coach Factory indigenously manufactured. 160 km/h speeds. 50+ services by 2024 connecting major cities. Part of Indian Railways modernisation.

nodes.label: National Education Policy 2020 (NEP)
nodes.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 29 July 2020, replaced 1986 NEP. Structural reform 5+3+3+4 (replacing 10+2). Mother tongue instruction till Class 5. Multidisciplinary higher education with multiple entry-exit points. Target: 6% GDP public education spend. National Research Foundation. PM SHRI schools scheme.

nodes.label: New Labour Codes (2019-20)
nodes.detail: Four labour codes consolidating 29 central laws: Code on Wages 2019, Industrial Relations Code 2020, Code on Social Security 2020, Occupational Safety Health and Working Conditions Code 2020. Universal minimum wage, inter-state migrants covered, gratuity portability. Implementation rules pending by states.

nodes.label: Aspirational Districts Programme (2018)
nodes.detail: Launched January 2018 by NITI Aayog. 112 most underdeveloped districts identified across 28 states. Real-time monitoring of health/nutrition, education, agriculture/water, financial inclusion, skill development, basic infrastructure via Champions of Change portal. Extended to Aspirational Blocks Programme January 2023 (500 blocks).

nodes.label: Look East → Act East Policy
nodes.detail: Look East Policy launched 1991 by PM Narasimha Rao to engage ASEAN + Japan + South Korea + Australia. Upgraded to Act East Policy 2014 by PM Modi — expanded to South Pacific, strategic partnerships. India-ASEAN FTA 2009 (goods), 2014 (services/investments). East Asia Summit participation.

nodes.label: Quad (Quadrilateral Security Dialogue)
nodes.detail: India-US-Japan-Australia grouping. Originated 2007 (tsunami relief), paused 2008, revived November 2017 at ASEAN Summit. First Leaders' Summit 12 March 2021 (virtual). In-person summits 2021 DC, 2022 Tokyo, 2023 Sydney/Hiroshima, 2024 Wilmington. Focus: Indo-Pacific, supply chains, vaccines, climate, critical tech.

nodes.label: I2U2 (India-Israel-UAE-USA)
nodes.detail: Minilateral grouping launched July 2022 at first Leaders' Summit. Focus: food security, water, energy, transportation, space, health, technology. UAE committed $2bn for integrated food parks in India. Pragmatic bloc bridging West Asia-South Asia.

nodes.label: IMEC (India-Middle East-Europe Corridor, 2023)
nodes.detail: India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor announced at G20 Delhi Summit 9 September 2023. India-UAE-Saudi Arabia-Jordan-Israel-Greece-EU. Rail + shipping + digital/electricity cables. Counter to China's BRI. Stalled by Israel-Hamas war October 2023.

nodes.label: Doklam Standoff (June-August 2017)
nodes.detail: 73-day military standoff at Doklam plateau (Bhutan-China disputed area) near India-Bhutan-China tri-junction. Started 16 June 2017 when Indian troops blocked Chinese road construction. Ended 28 August 2017 by mutual disengagement. Largest India-China standoff since 1962 until Galwan 2020.

nodes.label: Galwan Valley Clash (15 June 2020)
nodes.detail: Violent clash between Indian and Chinese troops in Galwan Valley, eastern Ladakh, 15-16 June 2020. First military casualties on India-China border since 1975. India lost 20 soldiers (Col Santoshi Babu), China 4+ (officially). Sparked Indian curbs on Chinese apps, FDI, PLI localisation push. Troop disengagement ongoing 2020-24 via 21+ rounds of Corps Commander talks.

nodes.label: Wuhan Informal Summit (April 2018)
nodes.detail: First informal summit between PM Modi and President Xi Jinping at Wuhan, 27-28 April 2018. Post-Doklam rapprochement. No joint statement; 'strategic guidance' exchanges on bilateral ties, border management, global issues. Paved way for Mamallapuram Summit 2019.

nodes.label: Mamallapuram/Chennai Informal Summit (October 2019)
nodes.detail: Second informal Modi-Xi summit at Mamallapuram (Mahabalipuram), Tamil Nadu, 11-12 October 2019. Discussed bilateral trade deficit, terrorism, India-China cultural links. Goodwill eroded by 2020 Galwan clash.

nodes.label: Operation Ganga (Feb-March 2022)
nodes.detail: Indian evacuation mission from Ukraine during Russia-Ukraine war. Started 26 February 2022. Evacuated ~22,500 Indians (mostly medical students) via Poland/Hungary/Romania/Slovakia/Moldova. Four Union Ministers dispatched as special envoys. Naveen Shekharappa, medical student, killed in Kharkiv shelling.

nodes.label: Operation Kaveri (Sudan, April 2023)
nodes.detail: Indian evacuation from Sudan during conflict between SAF and RSF. Launched 24 April 2023. Evacuated ~4,000 Indians via Port Sudan to Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. IAF C-130 Js and Indian Navy INS Sumedha used.

nodes.label: Vaccine Maitri (January 2021)
nodes.detail: India's COVID-19 vaccine diplomacy launched 20 January 2021. Supplied Covishield/Covaxin to 95+ countries — initial gifts + commercial + COVAX. Paused April 2021 due to Delta wave domestic demand; resumed Oct 2021. ~29+ crore doses exported by 2024.

nodes.label: Rafale Deal (France, 2016)
nodes.detail: Inter-Government Agreement signed 23 September 2016 for 36 Rafale fighter jets from Dassault Aviation (France). Rs 59,000 crore. First delivery October 2019 (Ambala). All 36 delivered by December 2022. Political controversy over pricing, offsets (Rahul Gandhi's 'chowkidar chor hai'). SC cleared deal Nov 2018.

nodes.label: S-400 Triumf Deal (Russia, 2018)
nodes.detail: Inter-Governmental Agreement signed 5 October 2018 by Modi-Putin for 5 S-400 air defence systems from Russia. Rs 35,000 crore. First squadron delivered November 2021, three operational by 2024. Covered potential CAATSA sanctions waiver concerns.

nodes.label: BrahMos Cruise Missile
nodes.detail: Indo-Russian supersonic cruise missile, joint venture DRDO + NPO Mashinostroyeniya. First launched 12 June 2001. Mach 2.8-3. Induction: Indian Navy (2005), Army (2007), Air Force (2017). Export: Philippines (2022, $375M — India's first major missile export). Range upgraded to 800 km post-MTCR entry (2016).

nodes.label: Agnipath Scheme (June 2022)
nodes.detail: Short-term military recruitment scheme announced 14 June 2022. 4-year tenure for Agniveers (17.5-21 years). 25% retained permanently; 75% exit with Rs 11.7L Seva Nidhi. Triggered violent protests across North India. First batch inducted January 2023. ~50,000 recruited annually.

nodes.label: NavIC / IRNSS (2018)
nodes.detail: Navigation with Indian Constellation, regional satellite navigation system. 7-satellite constellation (IRNSS-1A to 1G). Declared operational 2018. Coverage India + 1500 km. L5 + S band. NavIC chips mandatory in smartphones from 2023 in phases. Complement to GPS.

nodes.label: Astrosat (September 2015)
nodes.detail: India's first dedicated multi-wavelength space observatory. Launched 28 September 2015 by PSLV-C30. 5 instruments covering UV to X-ray. Studies binary stars, AGN, galaxies. Operational beyond design life. ISRO + TIFR + IUCAA + IIA + physical research lab.

nodes.label: Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act 2010
nodes.detail: Enacted 22 September 2010 to operationalise Indo-US Nuclear Deal. Capped operator liability at Rs 1,500 crore; supplier liability under Section 17(b) delayed reactor imports. Indian Nuclear Insurance Pool (INIP) 2015. Ratified Convention on Supplementary Compensation 2016.

nodes.label: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant
nodes.detail: India-Russia civil nuclear cooperation project at Kudankulam, Tamil Nadu. Units 1-2 (1000 MW each) operational 2013 & 2016. Units 3-6 under construction (Rostatom partnership). Protests 2011-13 over safety. Plant to have 6 VVER reactors total, 6000 MW capacity — India's largest.

nodes.label: India Semiconductor Mission (2021)
nodes.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 15 December 2021, launched 2022. Rs 76,000 crore outlay. Aims to build fabs (semiconductor manufacturing) + display fabs + compound semiconductors + ATMP. Major approvals: Tata Electronics (Dholera), CG Power, Micron (Sanand). Targets 2027 onwards.

nodes.label: IndiaAI Mission (March 2024)
nodes.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 7 March 2024. Rs 10,372 crore outlay. Seven pillars: Compute Capacity (10,000+ GPUs), IndiaAI Innovation Centre, Startup Financing, AI in Applications, Future Skills, IndiaAI Datasets Platform, Safe and Trusted AI. DPIIT + MeitY implementation.

nodes.label: Indian Space Policy 2023
nodes.detail: Approved by Union Cabinet 6 April 2023. Opened space sector to private players (NGEs — Non-Governmental Entities). ISRO focus shifts to R&D. IN-SPACe as single-window regulator. NSIL as commercial arm. Legislation (Space Activities Bill) pending.

nodes.label: National Health Mission (NHM, 2013)
nodes.detail: Launched 2013 merging NRHM (2005) + NUHM (2013). Accessible, affordable, quality healthcare to rural and urban areas. Indicators: IMR, MMR, TFR, CHC/PHC upgrades. Sub-missions: RMNCH+A, Communicable Diseases, Non-Communicable Diseases. ~70% of central health budget.

nodes.label: Mission Indradhanush (December 2014)
nodes.detail: Full immunisation coverage programme launched 25 December 2014. Targets unimmunised/partially immunised children (0-2 years) and pregnant women. Intensified (IMI) from 2017, IMI 2.0 (2019), 3.0 (2021). Raised full immunisation coverage from 62% (2014) to 87%+ (2023). 8+ vaccines in UIP.

nodes.label: Aarogya Setu App (April 2020)
nodes.detail: COVID-19 contact tracing + self-assessment mobile app launched 2 April 2020 by MyGov + NIC. Bluetooth/GPS based. 15+ crore downloads by May 2020. Linked to CoWIN for vaccine certificates. Privacy concerns addressed via Aarogya Setu Data Access and Knowledge Sharing Protocol.

nodes.label: Sonia Gandhi (Congress President 1998-2017, 2019-22)
nodes.detail: Italian-origin Indian politician. Widow of Rajiv Gandhi. Congress President 1998-2017 (19 years, longest ever) + 2019-22. MP Rae Bareli since 2004. Declined PM 2004. NAC chairperson. Credited with UPA-I policies (RTI, NREGA). Retreated from active politics 2022.

nodes.label: Rahul Gandhi (Congress, Leader of Opposition 2024-)
nodes.detail: Congress MP (Amethi 2004-19, Wayanad 2019-24, Rae Bareli 2024-). Congress President 2017-19. Led Bharat Jodo Yatra (Sept 2022 - Jan 2023, 4,000 km Kanyakumari to Srinagar). Bharat Jodo Nyay Yatra (Jan-Mar 2024). Leader of Opposition from June 2024 — first since 2014.

nodes.label: Arvind Kejriwal / Aam Aadmi Party (2012)
nodes.detail: Former IRS officer, RTI activist, Magsaysay 2006. Broke with Anna Hazare and founded AAP November 2012. Delhi CM (Dec 2013-Feb 2014, Feb 2015-Feb 2025). Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann. Resigned CM post after bail September 2024. Arrested in Delhi Liquor Policy case March 2024.

nodes.label: Nitish Kumar (Bihar CM)
nodes.detail: Bihar CM since 2005 (multiple terms). Alliance-hopping champion — switched between NDA and Mahagathbandhan 5+ times. JD(U) leader. Known for Bihar's law-and-order revival post-Lalu era and Patna Sahib women's reservation experiments.

nodes.label: Mamata Banerjee / Trinamool Congress
nodes.detail: TMC founder (1998), West Bengal CM since 2011 (three terms, first woman CM of WB). Former UPA Railway Minister. 2011 wrested WB from 34-year Left rule. 2021 victory despite Modi-Shah BJP challenge. Strong federalism advocate.

nodes.label: Naveen Patnaik (Odisha CM 2000-2024)
nodes.detail: BJD founder (1997), Odisha CM 5 March 2000 - 11 June 2024 (24 years — one of longest-serving). Lost 2024 to BJP (first BJP majority in Odisha). Cyclone response (Phailin 2013, Fani 2019, Amphan 2020). KALIA scheme, Odisha Millets Mission.

nodes.label: Yogi Adityanath (UP CM 2017-)
nodes.detail: BJP leader, Gorakhnath Math Mahant. Gorakhpur MP 1998-2017. Uttar Pradesh CM from 19 March 2017 (two terms). Flagship: law-and-order 'bulldozer raj', anti-Romeo squads, Purvanchal Expressway, Ram Mandir consecration.

nodes.label: Mayawati (UP CM 1995, 1997, 2002-03, 2007-12)
nodes.detail: Dalit politician, BSP President since 2003 (Kanshi Ram's successor). UP CM 4 times — 1995 (4 months), 1997 (6 months), 2002-03 (1 year), full 2007-12 (first BSP majority). Declined post-2017. Advocated Bahujan politics — SC/ST+OBC+Muslim coalition.

nodes.label: M.K. Stalin (Tamil Nadu CM 2021-)
nodes.detail: DMK President since 2018, Tamil Nadu CM from 7 May 2021. Son of M. Karunanidhi. Longtime Chennai Mayor (1996-2002). Led DMK's 2024 Lok Sabha INDIA bloc in TN (winning 22/39). Advocated fiscal federalism, opposed delimitation based on population.

nodes.label: Jaishri Laxmanrao Patil v. CoM Maharashtra (Maratha Reservation, 2021)
nodes.detail: 5-judge SC bench, 5 May 2021. Struck down Maharashtra's 16% Maratha reservation (SEBC Act 2018) as violative of Indra Sawhney 50% ceiling. Held 102nd Amendment deprived states of power to identify SEBCs — overturned by 105th Amendment (August 2021). Landmark on state power over OBC list.

nodes.label: Anoop Baranwal v. UOI (CEC Appointment, 2023)
nodes.detail: 5-judge SC Constitution Bench, 2 March 2023. Ruled CEC/EC appointments must be by committee of PM + LoP + CJI until Parliament legislates. Parliament enacted CEC and Other Election Commissioners Act 2023 to replace CJI with a Union Minister — controversial as diluting SC's intent.

nodes.label: Supriyo v. UOI (Marriage Equality, 2023)
nodes.detail: 5-judge SC bench, 17 October 2023. Unanimous refusal to grant legal recognition to same-sex marriages (3-2 on civil union). Held marriage falls within legislative domain, not judicial. Recommended committee for entitlements/benefits. Setback for LGBTQ+ marriage rights post-Navtej 2018.

nodes.label: Bilkis Bano Case (Convict Release 2022 → SC reversal 2024)
nodes.detail: 11 convicts (2002 Gujarat riots rape-murder of Bilkis Bano + her family) released by Gujarat government August 2022 under 1992 remission policy. SC bench (Justice Nagarathna) on 8 January 2024 quashed remission as illegal — Maharashtra (trial state) had jurisdiction, not Gujarat. Convicts returned to prison.

nodes.label: Vishaka Guidelines 1997 → POSH Act 2013
nodes.detail: 12-point guidelines by Supreme Court in Vishaka v. Rajasthan (August 1997) for preventing sexual harassment at workplace — borrowing from CEDAW. Internal Complaints Committees. Codified into Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act 2013 (POSH).

nodes.label: Subhash Chandra Agrawal v. CPIO (2009)
nodes.detail: Delhi HC ruled CJI's office falls under RTI Act 2005. Upheld 2019 by SC 5-judge bench. Required disclosure of judges' asset declarations. Strengthened judicial transparency while preserving collegium deliberation privilege.

nodes.label: Women Army Officers Permanent Commission (2020)
nodes.detail: SC bench, 17 February 2020 (Babita Puniya case). Granted permanent commission to women officers in 10 Army cadres (earlier only Short Service Commission up to 14 years). Similar rulings for Navy (Feb 2020), Air Force follow-on. Ended decades-long gender discrimination in military career progression.

nodes.label: 14th Finance Commission (Y.V. Reddy, 2015-20)
nodes.detail: Chaired by former RBI Governor Y.V. Reddy. Report submitted December 2014 for 2015-20. Raised states' share of central tax pool from 32% to 42% — biggest devolution increase ever. New horizontal distribution formula (population 2011, income distance, forest cover, demographic change, area).

nodes.label: 15th Finance Commission (N.K. Singh, 2020-26)
nodes.detail: Chaired by N.K. Singh. Two reports — 2020-21 (one year), 2021-26 (five years). States' share kept at 41% (1% withdrawn for new UTs J&K/Ladakh). New weights — demographic performance (12.5%) + tax effort (2.5%) introduced. Health grants. Revenue deficit grants.

nodes.label: 16th Finance Commission (Arvind Panagariya, 2026-31)
nodes.detail: Chaired by Arvind Panagariya (former NITI Aayog VC), constituted 31 December 2023. Report due 31 October 2025 for period 1 April 2026 - 31 March 2031. Key issues: demographic shifts, revenue-raising capacity, cess/surcharge controversy, GST compensation expiry.

nodes.label: Forest (Conservation) Amendment Act 2023
nodes.detail: Passed 2023, renamed Van (Sanrakshan Evam Samvardhan) Adhiniyam. Exempted forest land within 100 km of LAC/LoC from prior approval for strategic projects. Exempted land up to 10 hectares for linear projects, 5 hectares for security. Controversial dilution of Forest Conservation Act 1980 scope.

nodes.label: Wildlife (Protection) Amendment Act 2022
nodes.detail: Passed December 2022. Rationalised WPA 1972 schedules from 6 to 4. Enhanced CITES compliance (new schedule for CITES species). Standing Committee of NBWL. Stricter penalties. Notable: vermin declaration power retained with states.

nodes.label: Single-Use Plastic Ban (1 July 2022)
nodes.detail: Ban on manufacture, import, stocking, distribution, sale, use of 19 single-use plastic items from 1 July 2022 under Plastic Waste Management Amendment Rules 2021. Includes straws, cutlery, earbuds, ice-cream sticks, balloon sticks, wrapping films. Carry bags <120 microns banned from 31 Dec 2022.

nodes.label: Sovereign Green Bonds (2023)
nodes.detail: India's first Sovereign Green Bonds issued 25 January and 9 February 2023. Rs 16,000 crore raised (both tranches). 5-year and 10-year tenors. Proceeds for renewable energy, energy efficiency, clean transportation, sustainable water management. Listed on BSE/NSE; FPI access permitted.

nodes.label: GIFT City + IFSCA (2019)
nodes.detail: Gujarat International Finance Tec-City (GIFT City), India's first IFSC (International Financial Services Centre) in Gandhinagar. Operationalised 2015. IFSCA (International Financial Services Centres Authority) established 2019 as unified regulator. Aircraft leasing, bullion exchange, GIFT Nifty futures.

nodes.label: National Asset Reconstruction Company (NARCL, 2021)
nodes.detail: 'Bad Bank' launched 2021. PSBs' ARC to aggregate stressed assets >Rs 500 crore. NARCL + IDRCL (management) model. Rs 50,335 crore first tranche approved September 2021. Took over Srei Infra, Future Retail, Jaypee Infratech debts.

nodes.label: Crypto / VDA Tax Regime (2022)
nodes.detail: Budget 2022-23 introduced 30% flat tax on Virtual Digital Assets (crypto, NFTs) + 1% TDS (from 1 July 2022). No set-off against losses. Digital Rupee (CBDC) pilot launched November 2022 (wholesale) + December 2022 (retail). Registered with FIU-IND for AML compliance 2024.

nodes.label: Air India Privatisation (2022)
nodes.detail: Tata Group acquired Air India for Rs 18,000 crore, officially handed over 27 January 2022. First major PSU privatisation by Modi government. Tata regained airline it founded in 1932 and government nationalised 1953. Merged with Vistara (Feb 2025) to create consolidated Tata airline group.

nodes.label: Vivad Se Vishwas Scheme 2020
nodes.detail: Direct tax dispute resolution scheme, operational March 2020 - October 2021. Settle pending IT appeals by paying disputed tax (with waiver of interest, penalty, prosecution). Rs 99,756 crore collected from 1.46 lakh cases. Vivad Se Vishwas 2024 relaunched for pending disputes as of 22 July 2024.

nodes.label: Russia-Ukraine War (Feb 2022-)
nodes.detail: Russian invasion of Ukraine began 24 February 2022. India abstained at UNGA/UNSC resolutions condemning Russia. Refined Russian oil imports rose from 2% to 40%+ of imports. Grain Initiative through Turkey/UN. Over 1 lakh Indian casualties evacuated via Operation Ganga.

nodes.label: Israel-Hamas War (October 2023-)
nodes.detail: Hamas attack on Israel 7 October 2023 (1,200 killed, 240 hostages). Israel's Gaza offensive killed 40,000+ Palestinians by 2024. India condemned Hamas attack (first country to do so) + backed two-state solution. Complicated IMEC corridor progress. Gaza ceasefire January 2025.

nodes.label: Donald Trump Presidency-I (2017-21)
nodes.detail: 45th US President, 20 January 2017 - 20 January 2021. 'Howdy Modi' Houston Sept 2019. 'Namaste Trump' Ahmedabad Feb 2020. Trade tensions (GSP withdrawal 2019). Abraham Accords 2020. Withdrew from Paris Agreement, Iran Deal, TPP. Lost 2020 to Biden. Re-elected 2024 for second term.

nodes.label: Trump Presidency-II (January 2025-)
nodes.detail: 47th US President, inaugurated 20 January 2025. Tariff wars — 'Liberation Day' global tariffs April 2025 (India 26%). Withdrew from Paris Agreement, WHO again. Executive orders on immigration, federal workforce, AI. Modi visited Washington February 2025.

nodes.label: Arab Spring (2010-12)
nodes.detail: Revolutionary wave starting Tunisia December 2010 (Mohamed Bouazizi self-immolation). Egypt Tahrir Square 2011 (Mubarak fall); Libya (Gaddafi killed Oct 2011); Yemen; Syria civil war. India evacuated citizens from Libya, Egypt, Syria. Led to ISIS emergence.

nodes.label: Syrian Civil War (2011-24)
nodes.detail: Begin 2011 as Arab Spring uprising against Bashar al-Assad. ~500,000 killed, millions displaced. Russian intervention 2015 saved Assad. ISIS rose & fell (2014-19). Assad fell 8 December 2024 after HTS offensive — regime fled to Russia. Fragmented Syria 2025.

nodes.label: ISIS / Islamic State (2014-19)
nodes.detail: Declared caliphate 29 June 2014 under Abu Bakr al-Baghdadi. Controlled parts of Syria/Iraq incl. Mosul, Raqqa. Peak 2014-15. Territorial defeat March 2019 (Baghuz). Baghdadi killed Oct 2019. Ongoing insurgency in Syria/Iraq. ISKP (Khorasan) active in Afghanistan post-2021.

nodes.label: Brexit — UK leaves EU (31 January 2020)
nodes.detail: 2016 referendum (51.9% Leave). UK formally left EU 31 January 2020 after 47 years membership (joined EEC 1973). Transition period ended 31 December 2020 under Brexit deal. Triggered India-UK FTA negotiations (ongoing 2024-25).

nodes.label: Sri Lanka Economic Crisis (2022)
nodes.detail: Forex collapse April 2022, sovereign default May 2022 (first in SL history). Protests forced President Rajapaksa to flee July 2022. India's $4 bn financial assistance via credit lines, currency swap. IMF bailout $2.9 bn March 2023. Ranil Wickremesinghe → Anura Kumara Dissanayake (Sept 2024).

nodes.label: Three New States (November 2000)
nodes.detail: Chhattisgarh (carved from Madhya Pradesh, 1 November 2000), Uttarakhand (then Uttaranchal, carved from UP, 9 November 2000), Jharkhand (carved from Bihar, 15 November 2000). Tribal/regional demands. 27th, 28th, 29th states respectively. Increased total states to 28.

nodes.label: Telangana Formation (2 June 2014)
nodes.detail: 29th state of India carved from Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014. Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act 2014. Led by TRS (now BRS) under K. Chandrashekar Rao. Movement since 1969 (Jai Telangana). Hyderabad as joint capital for 10 years (till 2024). First CM: KCR. Congress won assembly elections Dec 2023 (Revanth Reddy).

nodes.label: J&K Reorganisation Act 2019
nodes.detail: J&K Reorganisation Act 2019, effective 31 October 2019. Bifurcated J&K state into UT of Jammu & Kashmir (with legislature) and UT of Ladakh (without legislature). First instance of a state downgraded to UT. Upheld by SC December 2023. Elections held September-October 2024.

nodes.label: Sarkaria Commission Report (1988)
nodes.detail: Commission on Centre-State Relations set up 1983, submitted report 1988. Chaired by former SC Justice R.S. Sarkaria. 247 recommendations on legislative, financial, administrative relations. Key: restrain Article 356, strengthen Inter-State Council, residuary powers. Many implemented gradually.

nodes.label: Punchhi Commission (2007-10)
nodes.detail: Second Commission on Centre-State Relations, set up April 2007 under former CJI M.M. Punchhi. Submitted 7-volume report March 2010. 310 recommendations — Art 356 use, Inter-State Council, grants-in-aid, AIS, communal violence, environment clearances. Partially implemented.

nodes.label: Justice Verma Committee (January 2013)
nodes.detail: Three-member committee chaired by former CJI J.S. Verma, constituted 23 December 2012 after Nirbhaya case. Report 23 January 2013. Recommended enhanced penalties for rape/sexual assault, new offences (acid attack, voyeurism, stalking), explicit recognition of marital rape exemption issue. Led to Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 2013.

nodes.label: Transgender Persons Act 2019
nodes.detail: Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act 2019, notified 10 January 2020. Self-identification principle (post-NALSA 2014 SC). National Council for Transgender Persons. Criminalises bonded labour, exclusion, denial of services. Criticised for mandatory district magistrate certificate.

nodes.label: NALSA v. UOI (Third Gender, 2014)
nodes.detail: 2-judge SC bench, 15 April 2014. Recognised transgender as 'third gender' under Article 14, 15, 16, 21. Right to self-identify. OBC reservation entitlement. Government obligations — social welfare, health, legal recognition. Basis for Transgender Persons Act 2019.

nodes.label: ICC Cricket World Cup 2011
nodes.detail: India won Cricket World Cup 2 April 2011 at Wankhede Stadium beating Sri Lanka. Captain M.S. Dhoni's six to win. Indian hosts (joint with Sri Lanka, Bangladesh). Tendulkar's last WC. Gautam Gambhir 97, Dhoni 91 in final. India's first WC since 1983.

nodes.label: India at Olympics (1996-2024)
nodes.detail: Medal count era 11: Leander Paes tennis bronze Atlanta 1996; Karnam Malleswari weightlifting bronze Sydney 2000 (first Indian woman medalist); Rajyavardhan Rathore shooting silver Athens 2004; Abhinav Bindra shooting gold Beijing 2008 (first individual gold). Peak London 2012 (6 medals), Rio 2016 (2), Tokyo 2020 (7 — Neeraj Chopra javelin gold), Paris 2024 (6).

nodes.label: Neeraj Chopra Javelin Gold (Tokyo Olympics 2021)
nodes.detail: First Indian athletics Olympic gold medal, won 7 August 2021 at Tokyo 2020 Olympics (held 2021). 87.58m throw. Silver at World Championships 2022, Gold 2023. Padma Shri 2022. Paris 2024 silver.

nodes.label: Amartya Sen Nobel Economics (1998)
nodes.detail: First Asian to win Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences, awarded October 1998 for work on welfare economics, social choice theory, poverty/famine, human development. Bharat Ratna 1999. Master of Trinity College Cambridge 1998-2004. Harvard Professor. HDI architect with Mahbub ul Haq.

nodes.label: Kailash Satyarthi Nobel Peace (2014)
nodes.detail: Indian children's rights activist, shared 2014 Nobel Peace Prize with Malala Yousafzai. Founded Bachpan Bachao Andolan (1980). Global March Against Child Labour 1998. Rescued 91,000+ children from bonded labour, trafficking. Advocate for education rights.

nodes.label: Abhijit Banerjee Nobel Economics (2019)
nodes.detail: Shared 2019 Nobel Economics with Esther Duflo (wife) and Michael Kremer for 'experimental approach to alleviating global poverty' (RCTs in development economics). Kolkata-born, MIT Ford Foundation Professor. Co-founded J-PAL.

nodes.detail: INC, BJP (1980), BSP (1984), SP (1992), TMC (1998), AIADMK, DMK, NCP (1999), RJD (1997), JD(U) (2003), JD(S), SS-UBT and Shiv Sena (split 2022), Biju Janata Dal BJD (1997), TRS→BRS (2001→2022), AIMIM, AAP (2012), TDP, YSRCP (2011), SS, CPM, CPI, NC, PDP, Akali Dal, IUML, RSP, KCM, Apna Dal, AIUDF, Lok Janshakti LJP.

nodes.label: Vinod Rai CAG Reports (2008-13)
nodes.detail: CAG (2008-2013). Exposed 2G spectrum scam (Rs 1.76 lakh crore presumptive loss, Nov 2010) + Coalgate (Rs 1.86 lakh crore, Aug 2012) + Commonwealth Games audit. Triggered UPA-II credibility crisis. Post-retirement: BCCI COA chair.

nodes.label: COVID-19 Delta Wave (April-June 2021)
nodes.detail: Catastrophic second wave April-June 2021 driven by Delta (B.1.617.2) variant. Daily cases peaked 400,000+ (7 May 2021). Oxygen shortage, crematorium queues, Ganga bodies. Estimated 3-5 million excess deaths (WHO). Kumbh Mela + WB elections super-spreaders. Vaccine push accelerated.
